member.name: M:Inventor.PresentationFace.CalculateFacetsWithOptions(System.Double,Inventor.NameValueMap,System.Int32@,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@,System.Double[]@,System.Int32[]@,System.Object@)
member.summary: Method that creates a new set of facets within the specified conditions.

param.name: ChordalTolerance
param.summary: Input Double that specifies the maximum distance that the facet can deviate from the smooth surface. This value is in centimeters. Smaller values can result in a much greater number of facets being returned and will require more processing time to calculate.

param.name: Options
param.summary: Input NameValueMap that specifies additional tolerances that can be used to control the output mesh. The supported options are: Name: MaxSideLength, Value: Defines the maximum side of any triangle in the mesh. A value of 0, or not supplying this value indicates that no maximum length is specified. Name: MaxAspectRatio, Value: Defines the maximum length to height ratio that a triangle can have. This helps to avoid long skinny triangles. A value of 0, or not supplying this value indicates that no maximum aspect ratio is specified. Name: MaxNormalDeviation, Value: Defines the maximum deviation between adjacent vertex normals. This value is the maximum angle allows between normals and is input as radians. A value of 0, or not supplying this value indicates that no normal deviation is specified. Name: ConversionMode, Value: Specifies the conversion mode (0 or 2). 0 - Do not convert the display mesh to a Quad-Dominant mesh. This mode instructs the faceter to keep the generated display mesh (i.e., skip the tri-mesh to quad-dominant mesh conversion). 2 - Convert the triangular display mesh to a triangular mesh suitable for STL output, 3D printing or other similar application requiring a slightly higher quality triangular mesh.

param.name: VertexCount
param.summary: Output Long that returns the number of vertices that were generated. This is the number of vertices that will be returned by the VertexCoordinates argument.

param.name: FacetCount
param.summary: Output Long that returns the number of facets that were generated.

param.name: VertexCoordinates
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that contains the coordinate locations of the vertices. The values are defined in x, y, z order within the array and represent coordinates within the model space of the faceted object.

param.name: NormalVectors
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that defines the normal for each vertex in the facet mesh. The values are defined in x, y, z order within the array and represent vector components within the model space of the faceted object.

param.name: VertexIndices
param.summary: Output array of Longs that are used as index values to index into the vertex coordinate list. The first coordinate in the vertex coordinate list is index 1. Using vertex indices allows vertex coordinates to be reused by more than one triangle, thus reducing the overall resources required to define the entire mesh.

param.name: TextureCoordinates
param.summary: Optional output array of Doubles that contains the coordinates of the texture map.

member.summary: Method that creates a new set of strokes within the specified conditions.

param.name: ChordalTolerance
param.summary: Input Double that specifies the maximum distance that the stroke can deviate from the smooth curve. This value is in centimeters. Smaller values can result in a much greater number of strokes being returned and will require more processing time to calculate.

param.name: Options
param.summary: Input NameValueMap that specifies additional tolerances that can be used to control the output strokes. param.name: PolylineCount
param.summary: Output Long that specifies the number of polylines that the strokes represent.

param.name: PolylineLengths
param.summary: Output array of Longs that specifies the number of vertices that are used to define each polyline.

member.summary: Provides access to all of the objects owned by a particular X and supports the methods to create additional Profiles. See the article in the overviews section.

member.name: M:Inventor.Profiles.AddForSolid(System.Boolean,System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that creates a profile containing multiple paths for creating solid features. The paths can include sketch curves as well as text boxes. Individual paths in the returned profile may be deleted to obtain the desired profile.

param.name: Combine
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether to combine the profile paths obtained when this method is used to create a new profile. For instance, let us take the example of a sketch containing two concentric circles. If this argument is specified to be true, the resulting profile will contain 2 profile paths, and the profile path corresponding to the inner circle will have its AddsMaterial flag set to False. Hence, the resulting profile is a circular disc with a circular cut\-out. If the Combine flag is specified to be False, the resulting profile will contain 2 profile paths with the AddsMaterial flag set to True for both paths. If the sketch contains text boxes, then the profile paths corresponding to them will always have the AddsMaterial flag set to True irrespective of whether the Combine flag is specified to be True or False.

param.name: ProfilePathSegments
param.summary: Optional input ObjectCollection that can contain sketch curves as well as text boxes. If sketch curves are specified, then the profile created by this method will include profile paths that are comprised of the exact set of sketch curves specified in the ObjectCollection. If text boxes are specified, then the profile created by this method will include profile paths that correspond to the exact set of text boxes specified in the ObjectCollection. Each text box in the collection will correspond to a unique profile path. If not specified, all the possible profile paths including sketch curves as well as text boxes will be included. This argument is ignored if the Combine argument is specified to be True.

param.name: Reserved
param.summary: Optional input Variant reserved for future use. This argument is currently ignored.

member.name: M:Inventor.Profiles.AddForSurface(System.Object)
member.summary: Method that creates a profile for creating surface features. The resulting profile could be open or closed.

param.name: Curve
param.summary: Optional input sketch curve. The method retrieves the end connected chain of entities that this curve is a part of and creates a profile. If not specified, the method will create a new profile by examining the contents of the sketch and creating a single connected path.

member.summary: Method that breaks the link between the project to surface curve and the model. This breaks the associativity to the model, allowing you to edit the individual sketch entities.

member.summary: Read-write property that gets and sets the sketch curves to project. Valid objects are 2D&3D sketch entities.

member.summary: Method that deletes the project to surface curve. This will delete all of the related sketch entities.

member.name: M:Inventor.ProjectToSurfaceCurve.Edit(Inventor.ObjectCollection,Inventor.ObjectCollection,System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that edits all of the inputs used to compute the project to surface curve. This method is more efficient than setting each of the individual properties since this will result in a single compute rather than computing after each property edit.

param.name: Faces
param.summary: Input ObjectCollection that specifies the faces and/or work planes to project curves to. Valid objects for this argument include Face and WorkPlane.

param.name: Curves
param.summary: Input ObjectCollection that specifies the curves to project. This can be one or more 2D/3D sketch entities, the sketch entities need not to be from the same sketch.

param.name: ProjectionType
param.summary: Optional input ProjectCurveToSufaceTypeEnum that specifies the projection type. If not specified this argument defaults to kProjectAlongVectorType and the PorjectDirection can be specified, and the Curves can include 2D&3D sketch entities. If kProjectToClosestPointType is specified the Curves can include 2D&3D sketch entities. If kWrapToFaceType is specified, the Faces should be developable faces, otherwise an error would occur. The Curves should include 2D sketch entities only.

param.name: ProjectDirection
param.summary: Optional input an object to specify the project direction. The direction is bidirectional. This is ignored if the ProjectionType is not specified as kProjectAlongVectorType. If not specified the normal of the sketch of first selected sketch curve is used. Valid objects are: · Linear Edge/WorkAxis, the direction of the edge is used. · Planar Face/WorkPlane, the normal of the face is used. · Cylindrical/conical/elliptical Face, the axis of the face is used.

member.name: P:Inventor.ProjectToSurfaceCurve.Faces
member.summary: Read-write property that defines the surfaces to project sketch curves to. The collection can contain Face and WorkPlane objects.

member.name: M:Inventor.ProjectToSurfaceCurve.GetReferenceKey(System.Byte[]@,System.Int32)
member.summary: Generate the sequence of bytes, called this object's reference key, which can be held onto beyond document edits and which will allow the caller to be bound back to the live object.

param.name: ReferenceKey
param.summary: Output array of Bytes that contains the reference key.

param.name: KeyContext
param.summary: Optional input Long that specifies the key context to use when creating the reference key. Although this argument is optional, you must currently always provide a valid key context. A key context is created using the CreateKeyContext method of the ReferenceKeyManager object.

member.summary: Method that creates a new custom PromptMessage.

param.name: Id
param.summary: Input the String value to specify the Id of PromptMessage. The Id should be unique in the collection of the PromptMessage objects.

param.name: PromptText
param.summary: Input the String value to specify the formatted prompt text of PromptMessage. The string can include “%s” to indicate a string placeholder that you can specify the string value for the placeholder using the PromptStrings argument in PromprMessage.Display method. Currently you can specify up to three placeholders. The string can also specify the hyperlink with XML tags.

param.name: Buttons
param.summary: Input the Long value to specify the buttons to use for PromptMessage. Valid values are: vbOKOnly or 0. vbOKCancel or 1. vbAbortRetryIgnore or 2. vbYesNoCancel or 3. vbYesNo or 4. vbRetryCancel or 5.

param.name: Icon
param.summary: Input Long that specifies the icon type. This can be vbCritical (16), vbExclamation (48), vbInformation(64) or vbQuestion (32).

param.name: Title
param.summary: Optional input String value to specify the title for PromptMessage. If not supplied, the title will default to "Inventor x", where x is the release number.

param.name: DisplayedPromptText
param.summary: Optional input String value to specify the displayed prompt text of PromptMessage. If not specified the PromptText will be used as DisplayedPromptText and displayed on Prompt Text column onto Prompts option, otherwise this DisplayedPromptText will be displayed instead. This can be set when the PromptText contains special chars that is not suitable to display in UI.

param.name: DefaultAnswer
param.summary: Optional input Long value to specify the default response for the PromptMessage dialog. Valid values are: vbDefaultButton1 (or 0) indicating the first button is set as default response button. This is also default value if not specified. vbDefaultButton2 (or 256) indicating the second button is set as default response button. vbDefaultButton3 (or 512) indicating the third button is set as default response button. If not supplied the first button will be set as default answer.

param.name: Restrictions
param.summary: Optional input Long(PromptMessageRestrictionsEnum) value to specify the “Controls when you will see this prompt” option for PromptMessage(grey out the options). Zero or more of the following, in combination (can be added together with +): kNoRestrictions (Allow all of the radio button options in the dialog "Do not show this message again ever", "Do not show this message again this session", "Prompt only once per operation", "Always show this message ", for all buttons) kDontAllowNeverAgain (Disable the "Do not show this message again ever" option) kDontAllowNoMoreThisSession (Disable the "Do not show this message again this session" option) Button 1 options (i.e. what is allowed/not allowed if button 1 is picked) : kDontAllowButton1NeverAgain (Disable the "Do not show this message again ever" option if button 1 is selected) kDontAllowButton1NoMoreThisSession (Disable the "Do not show this message again this session" option if button 1 is selected) Button 2 options (i.e. what is allowed/not allowed if button 2 is picked) : kDontAllowButton2NeverAgain (Disable the "Do not show this message again ever" option if button 2 is selected) kDontAllowButton2NoMoreThisSession (Disable the "Do not show this message again this session" option if button 2 is selected) Button 3 options (i.e. what is allowed/not allowed if button 3 is picked) : kDontAllowButton3NeverAgain (Disable the "Do not show this message again ever" option if button 3 is selected) kDontAllowButton3NoMoreThisSession (Disable the "Do not show this message again this session" option if button 3 is selected)

param.name: PromptSettings
param.summary:
Optional input NameValueMap object that specifies more prompt settings.
This is reserved for future use.

member.summary: Method that creates a punch note on the sheet based on the \input punch edge.

param.summary: Input Point2d that specifies the position of the punch note on the sheet.

param.name: PunchEdge
param.summary: Input GeometryIntent object that specifies the punch geomery to create the note for. The GeometryIntent object defines the geometry (typically a curve but can also be a center mark that represents the origin of a punch) and the location on the geometry where the note will point. If the GeometryIntent does not represent a punch edge or punch center, the method returns an error.

param.name: DimensionStyle
param.summary: Optional input Variant that specifies which dimension style to use for the note. The dimension style can be specified by providing the name of an existing style or by supplying a DimensionStyle object.

member.name: M:Inventor.PunchToolFeature.SetSuppressionCondition(Inventor.Parameter,Inventor.ComparisonTypeEnum,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that sets the suppression condition for the feature.

param.name: Parameter
param.summary: Parameter object that specifies the parameter whose value is to be checked for feature suppression.

param.name: ComparisonType
param.summary: ComparisonTypeEnum that specifies the type of comparison. Valid types are kEqualToComparison, kNotEqualToComparison, kLessThanComparison, kGreaterThanComparison, kLessThanOrEqualToComparison, kGreaterThanOrEqualToComparison.

param.name: Expression
param.summary: Specifies the expression used for the comparison with the parameter value. This can either be a string, a value or a parameter object. If a value is input, the database units for the units defined by the parameter are used. For instance, if the parameter defines length units, the value is assumed to be in centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current units of the document. For instance, if the parameter defines length units, the current length units of the document are used.

member.name: M:Inventor.PunchToolFeatures.Add(Inventor.ObjectCollection,Inventor.iFeatureDefinition,System.Object,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Creates a new PunchToolFeature using the input placement information.

param.name: PunchCenterPoints
param.summary: Input ObjectCollection of SketchPoint objects that define the placement position(s) of the punch tool. All of the supplied SketchPoint objects must be owned by the same sketch.

param.name: Definition
param.summary: Input iFeatureDefinition object used to define the various input required for the placement of a PunchToolFeature. Appropriate input must be defined in the iFeatureDefinition object in order to place the punch tool.

param.name: Angle
param.summary: Optional Input Variant that defines the placement angle of the punch tool. If not supplied, the punch tool will be placed with a rotation angle of zero. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are radians. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current angle units of the document.

param.name: AcrossBends
param.summary: Input Boolean specifies whether the punch tool feature goes across bends or not.

member.name: M:Inventor.RadiusModelDimension.GetDisplayGeometry(Inventor.Camera,System.Int32@,System.Int32[]@,System.Boolean[]@,System.Int32@,System.Int32[]@,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@)
member.summary: Method that returns simple linear geometry that represents the display geometry of the annotation. The result is returned as groups of connected lines (polylines). Groups can optionally be filled with internal voids.

param.name: Camera
param.summary: Input Camera object that specifies the view orientation. This can either be a transient Camera object or that got from View object etc.. And the camera properties can be changed but not applied.

param.name: GroupCount
param.summary: Output Long that indicates the number of groups. A group is a set of related polylines where there can be one outer and multiple inner polylines. Groups can optionally also be filled.

param.name: PolylinesPerGroup
param.summary: Output array of Longs that indicates the number of polylines in each of the groups. The array size will be GroupCount where each value of this array indicates the number of polylines within each group. When reading the polylines within a group, the first polyline is the outer polyline and any additional closed polylines represent internal voids if the group is filled.

param.name: FilledGroups
param.summary: Output array of Booleans that indicates which groups are filled. A value of True indicates the corresponding group is filled. The array size will be GroupCount. If a group is filled, the first polyline in the group defines the outer loop. Any other polylines for that group represent internal loops and voids in the fill.

param.name: PolylineCount
param.summary: Output Long that indicates the total number of polylines.

param.name: PolylineLengths
param.summary: Output array of Longs that indicates the number of vertices used in each polyline.

param.name: VertexCount
param.summary: Output Long that indicates the total number of vertices.

param.name: VertexCoordinates
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that contains the coordinates.

member.name: M:Inventor.RadiusModelDimension.GetFilledAreaFacetsInfo(Inventor.Camera,System.Int32@,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@,System.Int32[]@,System.Int32@,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@,System.Int32[]@)
member.summary: Returns facets’ coordinates of the filled areas of the annotation.

param.name: Camera
param.summary: Input Camera object that specifies the view orientation. This can either be a transient Camera object or that got from View object etc.. And the camera properties can be changed but not applied.

param.name: TextVertexCount
param.summary: Output Long value that indicates vertex count of filled texts.

param.name: TextFacetCount
param.summary: Output Long value that indicates facet count of filled texts.

param.name: TextVertexCoordinates
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that indicates the vertices coordinates of the filled texts. The array is a single dimension array containing sequential x, y, z values.

param.name: TextVertexIndices
param.summary: Output array of Longs that are used as index values to index into the filled text vertex coordinate list. The first coordinate in the vertex coordinate list is index 1. Using vertex indices allows vertex coordinates to be reused by more than one triangle, thus reducing the overall resources required to define the entire mesh.

param.name: SymbolVertexCount
param.summary: Output Long value that indicates vertex count of filled symbols.

param.name: SymbolFacetCount
param.summary: Output Long value that indicates facet count of filled symbols.

param.name: SymbolVertexCoordinates
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that indicates the vertices coordinates of the filled symbols. The array is a single dimension array containing sequential x, y, z values.

param.name: SymbolVertexIndices
param.summary: Output array of Longs that are used as index values to index into the filled symbol vertex coordinate list. The first coordinate in the vertex coordinate list is index 1. Using vertex indices allows vertex coordinates to be reused by more than one triangle, thus reducing the overall resources required to define the entire mesh.

member.name: M:Inventor.RadiusModelDimensionProxy.GetDisplayGeometry(Inventor.Camera,System.Int32@,System.Int32[]@,System.Boolean[]@,System.Int32@,System.Int32[]@,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@)
member.summary: Method that returns simple linear geometry that represents the display geometry of the annotation. The result is returned as groups of connected lines (polylines). Groups can optionally be filled with internal voids.

param.name: Camera
param.summary: Input Camera object that specifies the view orientation. This can either be a transient Camera object or that got from View object etc.. And the camera properties can be changed but not applied.

param.name: GroupCount
param.summary: Output Long that indicates the number of groups. A group is a set of related polylines where there can be one outer and multiple inner polylines. Groups can optionally also be filled.

param.name: PolylinesPerGroup
param.summary: Output array of Longs that indicates the number of polylines in each of the groups. The array size will be GroupCount where each value of this array indicates the number of polylines within each group. When reading the polylines within a group, the first polyline is the outer polyline and any additional closed polylines represent internal voids if the group is filled.

param.name: FilledGroups
param.summary: Output array of Booleans that indicates which groups are filled. A value of True indicates the corresponding group is filled. The array size will be GroupCount. If a group is filled, the first polyline in the group defines the outer loop. Any other polylines for that group represent internal loops and voids in the fill.

param.name: PolylineCount
param.summary: Output Long that indicates the total number of polylines.

param.name: PolylineLengths
param.summary: Output array of Longs that indicates the number of vertices used in each polyline.

param.name: VertexCount
param.summary: Output Long that indicates the total number of vertices.

param.name: VertexCoordinates
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that contains the coordinates.

member.name: M:Inventor.RadiusModelDimensionProxy.GetFilledAreaFacetsInfo(Inventor.Camera,System.Int32@,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@,System.Int32[]@,System.Int32@,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@,System.Int32[]@)
member.summary: Returns facets’ coordinates of the filled areas of the annotation.

param.name: Camera
param.summary: Input Camera object that specifies the view orientation. This can either be a transient Camera object or that got from View object etc.. And the camera properties can be changed but not applied.

param.name: TextVertexCount
param.summary: Output Long value that indicates vertex count of filled texts.

param.name: TextFacetCount
param.summary: Output Long value that indicates facet count of filled texts.

param.name: TextVertexCoordinates
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that indicates the vertices coordinates of the filled texts. The array is a single dimension array containing sequential x, y, z values.

param.name: TextVertexIndices
param.summary: Output array of Longs that are used as index values to index into the filled text vertex coordinate list. The first coordinate in the vertex coordinate list is index 1. Using vertex indices allows vertex coordinates to be reused by more than one triangle, thus reducing the overall resources required to define the entire mesh.

param.name: SymbolVertexCount
param.summary: Output Long value that indicates vertex count of filled symbols.

param.name: SymbolFacetCount
param.summary: Output Long value that indicates facet count of filled symbols.

param.name: SymbolVertexCoordinates
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that indicates the vertices coordinates of the filled symbols. The array is a single dimension array containing sequential x, y, z values.

param.name: SymbolVertexIndices
param.summary: Output array of Longs that are used as index values to index into the filled symbol vertex coordinate list. The first coordinate in the vertex coordinate list is index 1. Using vertex indices allows vertex coordinates to be reused by more than one triangle, thus reducing the overall resources required to define the entire mesh.

member.name: M:Inventor.RectangularPatternFeatures.CreateDefinition(Inventor.ObjectCollection,System.Object,System.Boolean,System.Object,System.Object,Inventor.PatternSpacingTypeEnum)
member.summary: Method that creates a new RectangularPatternFeatureDefinition object.

param.name: ParentFeatures
param.summary: Input ObjectCollection object that contains the features or solids to be patterned. The collection could contain the various part features, sheet metal features, work planes, work axes, work points, or SurfaceBody objects. If SurfaceBody objects are supplied, the only other objects that can be in the collection are work planes, work axes, work points, and surface part features.

param.name: XDirectionEntity
param.summary: Input a linear entity that defines the first direction. This can be a linear Edge, a WorkAxis, a WorkPlane (normal is used), a planar Face (normal is used), or a GeometryIntent. When input GeometryIntent the geometry can be a non-linear Edge or Path, and the intent is used to specify a point on the geometry and the tangent direction at the point of the geometry will be used as the X-direction of the pattern feature.Use the CreatePath or CreateSpecifiedPath methods on the PartFeatures object to create a Path. The path can be a combination of 2D and 3D sketch elements.

param.name: NaturalXDirection
param.summary: Input Boolean that indicates if the direction of the pattern is in the natural direction of the XDirectionEntity or reversed. A value of True indicates it is in the natural direction.

param.name: XCount
param.summary: Input Variant that defines the number of instances in the X direction. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter will be created to control this value when the feature is created. If a string is input it can be any string that can be evaluated by Inventor to result in a unitless number.

param.name: XSpacing
param.summary: Input Variant that defines the spacing between instances in the X direction. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter will be created to control this value when the feature is created. If a string is input it can be any string that can be evaluated by Inventor to result in a unitless number. This input may be left unspecified only if the XSpacingType is kFitToPathLength and if the XDirectionEntity is not a work axis.

param.name: XSpacingType
param.summary: Optional input PatternSpacingTypeEnum enum that indicates if the occurrences along the x direction are to be fitted within a specified distance. A value of kDefault indicates that the occurrences are to be separated by the specified distance. A value of kFitted indicates that all occurrences are to be fitted within the specified distance. A value of kFitToPathLength indicates that all occurrences are to be fitted within a distance equal to the length of the XDirectionEntity. The kFitToPathLength value is invalid in cases where the XDirectionEntity is a work axis.

member.name: M:Inventor.ReferenceFeature.SetSuppressionCondition(Inventor.Parameter,Inventor.ComparisonTypeEnum,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that sets the suppression condition for the feature.

param.name: Parameter
param.summary: Parameter object that specifies the parameter whose value is to be checked for feature suppression.

param.name: ComparisonType
param.summary: ComparisonTypeEnum that specifies the type of comparison. Valid types are kEqualToComparison, kNotEqualToComparison, kLessThanComparison, kGreaterThanComparison, kLessThanOrEqualToComparison, kGreaterThanOrEqualToComparison.

param.name: Expression
param.summary: Specifies the expression used for the comparison with the parameter value. This can either be a string, a value or a parameter object. If a value is input, the database units for the units defined by the parameter are used. For instance, if the parameter defines length units, the value is assumed to be in centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current units of the document. For instance, if the parameter defines length units, the current length units of the document are used.

member.name: M:Inventor.ReferenceKeyEvents.OnBindKeyToObject(System.Byte[]@,System.Object,System.Object@,Inventor.SolutionNatureEnum@,Inventor.NameValueMap,Inventor.HandlingCodeEnum@)
member.summary: Event that fires when either the BindKeyToObject or CanBindKeyToObject method of the ReferenceKeyManager object is called with a custom reference key.

param.name: ReferenceKey
param.summary: Input array of Bytes that contains the reference key.

param.name: Document
param.summary: The document object that the client obtained the ReferenceKeyManager object from and called the BindKeyToObject or CanBindKeyToObject method.

param.name: Object
param.summary: Output object that was found as a result of binding the provided reference key. The initial value of this argument is Nothing. In the case of multiple matches, the client should return an ObjectCollection containing all the candidate matches. The primary match is always the first member of this collection. Except for the first element, the order is not significant.

param.name: MatchType
param.summary: Output SolutionNatureEnum that returns the nature of the solution that was found.

param.name: Context
param.summary: Not currently used.

param.name: HandlingCode
param.summary: Output that indicates if you are handling the event. kEventNotHandled indicates that the reference key is not yours and you’re not handling the binding. kEventHandled indicates that the reference key is yours and you are handling the binding. Even if the binding is unsuccessful you should return kEventHandled but with a match type of kNoSolution.

member.summary: Method to bind a reference key to the persistent object within the document. Returns a specific object, if there is a unique solution.

param.summary: Input Long that specifies the key context to use. This must reference the same context data that was used when the key was originally generated. param.name: MatchType
param.summary: Output SolutionNatureEnum that returns the nature of the solution that was found.

member.name: M:Inventor.ReferenceKeyManager.CanBindKeyToObject(System.Byte[]@,System.Int32,System.Object@,System.Object@)
member.summary: Method that returns whether the key can be bound to an entity or not.

param.name: ReferenceKey
param.summary: Array of bytes that contains a reference key.

param.name: KeyContext
param.summary: Input Long that specifies the key context to use. This must reference the same context data that was used when the key was originally generated. The key context must be supplied when working with any B-Rep entities (SurfaceBody, Face, Edge, etc.). For other entity types it is ignored.

param.name: Object
param.summary: Optional output object that returns the object if the bind was successful. An ObjectCollection is returned if multiple matches are found. Returns Nothing if the method returns False.

param.name: Context
param.summary: Optional output NameValueMap object that returns information about the binding process. Possible values: ObjectSuppressed As Boolean. Indicates whether the bind failed because the object is in a suppressed occurrence. ObjectMissing As Boolean. Indicates whether the bind failed because the object is in a missing (unresolved) occurrence. ObjectDeleted As Boolean. Indicates whether the bind failed because the object is in a deleted occurrence. KnownOccurrencePath As ComponentOccurrence. Contains the known occurrence path in which the object lives. MatchType As SolutionNatureEnum. Contains the nature of the solution if found.

member.name: M:Inventor.RepresentationEvents.OnDelete(Inventor.Document,System.Object,Inventor.EventTimingEnum,Inventor.NameValueMap,Inventor.HandlingCodeEnum@)
member.summary: The OnDelete event notifies the client when any representation related objects are deleted. These include positional representations and design views.

param.name: DocumentObject
param.summary: The Document object the deleted object is within.

param.name: Entity
param.summary: The representation that is being deleted. When the value of the BeforeOrAfter argument is kBefore, the object provided is the object before being deleted. When the value is kAfter, an object is also provided but since the actual entity has been deleted calling any methods or properties on the object will fail. The only thing that is valid to do with the object at this time is to compare it's identity with a reference previously saved. For example: Private m_oDeletedEntity As Object Private Sub oRepresentationEvents_OnDelete(ByVal DocumentObject As Document, ByVal Entity As Object, ByVal BeforeOrAfter As EventTimingEnum, ...) If BeforeOrAfter = kBefore Then ' Somehow Check to see if the representation being deleted is an interesting one. If Interesting(Entity) Then ' Save a reference to the object. Set m_oDeletedEntity = Entity End If Else ' Now we're either after the delete or it's been aborted. ' Check to see if the object is the interesting one. If Entity is m_oDeletedEntity Then If BeforeOrAfter = kAfter then ' The object was deleted. ElseIf BeforeOrAfter = kAbort Then ' The delete was aborted. End If End If End Sub

param.name: BeforeOrAfter
param.summary: Input EventTimingEnum indicating when the event is being fired. Notification is sent before and after the object is deleted.

param.name: Context
param.summary: Input NameValueMap object that can be used to determine the context of why the event fired. No context information is provided for this event.

param.name: HandlingCode
param.summary: Output HandlingCodeEnum that indicates how you are handling the event. The value of this argument is currently ignored for this event.

member.name: M:Inventor.RepresentationEvents.OnNewSectionView(Inventor.Document,Inventor.DesignViewRepresentation,Inventor.EventTimingEnum,Inventor.NameValueMap,Inventor.HandlingCodeEnum@)
member.summary: Event that is fired whenever an section view is created in part or assembly.

param.name: DocumentObject
param.summary: Input Document object that indicates the document in which the change occurred.

param.name: Representation
param.summary: Input DesignViewRepresentation object that the section view is created in.

param.name: BeforeOrAfter
param.summary: Input EventTimingEnum indicating if the event is being fired before (kBefore) or after (kAfter) the section view is created. This notification is currently only provided after the section view is created so this is always kAfter.

param.name: Context
param.summary:
Input NameValueMap object that can be used to determine the context of why the event fired. Additional information is provided through this argument to help in understanding the context of the notification.

Name = “SectionViewType”. Value = A value from SectionViewTypeEnum that indicates which type of section view is just created or section view is ended.

Name = “FirstSectionPlane”. Value = A Plane object that indicates the first section plane for quarter or three quarter section view and the section plane for the half section view. The normal of the section plane defines the section direction.

Name = “SecondSectionPlane”. Value = A Plane object that indicates the second section plane for quarter or three quarter section view. The normal of the section plane defines the section direction.

param.name: HandlingCode
param.summary: Output HandlingCodeEnum that indicates how you are handling the event. The value of this argument is currently ignored for this event.

member.summary: Property returning the parent WorkAxis object.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolvedFaceWorkAxisDef.Type

member.name: T:Inventor.RevolveFeature
member.summary: The RevolveFeature object represents revolved modeling features. The properties and methods listed below are in addition to those supported by the Feature object.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.Adaptive
member.summary: Gets and sets whether this feature is adaptive or not.

member.name: M:Inventor.RevolveFeature.AddParticipant(Inventor.ComponentOccurrence)
member.summary: Method that adds the specified participant to the assembly feature. This method fails for features in a part.

param.name: Occurrence
param.summary: ComponentOccurrence object that specifies the participant to be added. An error occurs if the input ComponentOccurrence is not a leaf occurrence.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.Appearance
member.summary: Gets and sets the current appearance of the feature.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.AppearanceSourceType
member.summary: Gets and sets the source of the appearance for the feature.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.Application
member.summary: Returns the top-level parent application object. When used the context of Inventor, an Application object is returned. When used in the context of Apprentice, an ApprenticeServer object is returned.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.AttributeSets
member.summary: Property that returns the AttributeSets collection object associated with this object.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.AxisEntity
member.summary: Gets and sets the entity used to define the axis of revolution.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.ConsumeInputs
member.summary: Gets and sets whether the inputs to this feature should be nested under this feature in the browser.

member.name: M:Inventor.RevolveFeature.Delete(System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that deletes the feature. The arguments allow control over which dependent objects are also deleted.

param.name: RetainConsumedSketches
param.summary: Optional input Boolean indicating if consumed sketches within the feature should be deleted. If the feature being deleted is not a sketch based feature this argument is ignored.

param.name: RetainDependentFeaturesAndSketches
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies if dependent features should be deleted. If there are no dependent features this argument is ignored.

param.name: RetainDependentWorkFeatures
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies if dependent work features should be deleted. If there are no dependent work features this argument is ignored.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.EndFaces
member.summary: Property that returns the set of that cap one end of the revolution that are coincident with the sketch plane. The end faces are those not coincident to the sketch plane of the feature's profile. In the case of a symmetric revolution these faces are the ones on the negative normal side of the sketch plane. In the cases where there aren't any end faces this property will return Nothing.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.ExtendedName
member.summary: Read-only property that returns the full feature name including any extended information.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.Extent
member.summary: Property that returns the object that defines how the extent of the feature is defined. The type of extent object that this property will return can be determined by using the ExtentType property.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.ExtentTwo
member.summary: Property that returns the PartFeatureExtent object that defines how the second direction extent of the feature is defined. The type of extent object returned can be determined by using the ExtentTwoType property. This property returns Nothing if the IsTwoDirectional property returns False.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.ExtentTwoType
member.summary: Property that returns an enum indicating how the second direction extent of the feature is defined. This indicates the type of object returned by the Extent property. This property returns a failure if the IsTwoDirectional property \returns False.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.ExtentType
member.summary: Property that returns an enum indicating how the extent of the feature is defined. This indicates the type of object returned by the Extent property. The valid possibilities returned are kAngleExtent and kFullSweepExtent.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.Faces
member.summary: Property that returns a collection that provides access to all of the faces of the feature. The Faces collection object will return the faces that still currently exist in the part. For example, if a face has been consumed by additional modeling operations it will not be returned.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.FeatureDimensions
member.summary: Property that returns the FeatureDimensions collection object.

member.name: M:Inventor.RevolveFeature.GetReferenceKey(System.Byte[]@,System.Int32)
member.summary: Method that generates and returns the reference key for this entity.

param.name: ReferenceKey
param.summary: Input/output array of Bytes that contains the reference key.

param.name: KeyContext
param.summary: Input Long that specifies the key context. The key context must be supplied when working with any B-Rep entities (and SurfaceBody, FaceShell, Face, Edge, EdgeUse and Vertex objects). A key context is created using the CreateKeyContext method of the ReferenceKeyManager object. For all other object types, the key context argument is not used and is ignored if provided.

member.name: M:Inventor.RevolveFeature.GetSuppressionCondition(Inventor.Parameter@,Inventor.ComparisonTypeEnum@,System.Object@)
member.summary: Method that gets the suppression condition for the feature. The method returns False if no condition has been applied.

param.name: Parameter
param.summary: Parameter object that specifies the parameter whose value is to be checked for feature suppression.

param.name: ComparisonType
param.summary: ComparisonTypeEnum that specifies the type of comparison. Valid return types are kEqualToComparison, kNotEqualToComparison, kLessThanComparison, kGreaterThanComparison, kLessThanOrEqualToComparison, kGreaterThanOrEqualToComparison.

param.name: Expression
param.summary: Specifies the expression used for the comparison with the parameter value. This can either be a string or a parameter object.

member.name: P:Inventor.RevolveFeature.HealthStatus

member.summary: Property that returns whether extents have been defined in two directions for the revolve. If this property returns True, the ExtentTwoType and ExtentTwo properties can be used to query details about the second direction extent.

member.name: M:Inventor.RevolveFeature.SetAngleExtent(System.Object,Inventor.PartFeatureExtentDirectionEnum)
member.summary: Method that changes the extents of the revolution to the given angle

param.name: Angle
param.summary: Defines the sweep angle of the revolution. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are radians. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current angle units of the document.

param.name: ExtentDirection
param.summary: constant that indicates the direction of the sweep. Valid input is kPositive, kNegative, or kSymmetric. The sweep direction is defined relative to the natural direction of the axis entity. kPositive defines the sweep to be in a positive direction using the right-hand rule about the axis.

member.name: M:Inventor.RevolveFeature.SetEndOfPart(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that repositions the end-of-part marker relative to the object this method is called from.

param.name: Before
param.summary: Input Boolean that indicates if the end of part marker should be immediately before or after this work feature. A value of True indicates before and False indicates after.

member.name: M:Inventor.RevolveFeature.SetFromToExtent(System.Object,System.Boolean,System.Object,System.Boolean,Inventor.PartFeatureExtentDirectionEnum,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that changes the extents to be 'from and to face' extents.

param.name: FromFace
param.summary: Input Object that defines the 'from face'. This can be either a Face or WorkPlane object.

param.name: ExtendFromFace
param.summary: Input Boolean that defines whether the 'from face' should be extended to contain the extents of the profile.

param.name: ToFace
param.summary: Input Object that defines the 'to face'. This can be either a Face or WorkPlane object.

param.name: ExtendToFace
param.summary: Input Boolean that defines whether the 'to face' should be extended to contain the extents of the profile.

param.name: ExtentDirection
param.summary: Input constant that indicates which side of the sketch plane to extrude towards. Valid input is kPositiveExtentDirection or kNegativeExtentDirection. kPositiveExtentDirection defines the offset direction to be in the same direction as the normal of the sketch plane.

param.name: MinimumSolution
param.summary: Input Boolean that defines whether the feature terminates on the nearest valid face when there are multiple options for valid termination faces.

member.name: M:Inventor.RevolveFeature.SetFullExtent
member.summary: Method that changes the angle of the revolve to a full (360-degree) revolution.

member.name: M:Inventor.RevolveFeature.SetSuppressionCondition(Inventor.Parameter,Inventor.ComparisonTypeEnum,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that sets the suppression condition for the feature.

param.name: Parameter
param.summary: Parameter object that specifies the parameter whose value is to be checked for feature suppression.

param.name: ComparisonType
param.summary: ComparisonTypeEnum that specifies the type of comparison. Valid types are kEqualToComparison, kNotEqualToComparison, kLessThanComparison, kGreaterThanComparison, kLessThanOrEqualToComparison, kGreaterThanOrEqualToComparison.

param.name: Expression
param.summary: Specifies the expression used for the comparison with the parameter value. This can either be a string, a value or a parameter object. If a value is input, the database units for the units defined by the parameter are used. For instance, if the parameter defines length units, the value is assumed to be in centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current units of the document. For instance, if the parameter defines length units, the current length units of the document are used.

param.name: MinimumSolution

param.summary: Input Variant that defines the sweep angle of the revolution. This can be either a numeric value or a string. member.name: M:Inventor.RibbonPanels.Add(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that creates a new RibbonPanel within a ribbon tab. The newly created RibbonPanel is returned.

param.name: DisplayName
param.summary: Input string that defines the display name of the ribbon panel. This is the name that is displayed to the user and should be localized for different locales.

param.name: InternalName
param.summary: Input string that defines the unique internal name of the ribbon panel. This is the internal name and is not displayed to the user. The name must be unique with respect to all other ribbon panels within the tab. The name should remain constant in all locales so it can be used to find a specific panel.

param.name: ClientId
param.summary: Input String that uniquely identifies the client. This is the CLSID of the AddIn in a string form, e.g. "{C9A6C580\-3817\-11D0\-BE4E\-080036E87B02}". If supplied, this string is used at Inventor start up time to determine whether the AddIn that created this ribbon panel has since been uninstalled. If so, the panel is deleted.The string is also used to find all the panels to delete when the associated Add\-in is unloaded. A 'dummy' string or a null string can be specified, but is not recommended.

param.name: TargetPanelInternalName
param.summary: Optional input String that specifies the internal name of an existing panel to position the new panel next to. If specified, the InsertBeforeTargetPanel argument indicates whether to place the new panel before or after the target panel. If not specified, the new panel is positioned at the end.

param.name: InsertBeforeTargetPanel
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether to position the new panel before or after the target ribbon panel. The argument defaults to False and is not used if the TargetPanelInternalName argument is not specified.

param.summary: Optional input String that specifies the internal name of an existing tab to position the new tab next to. param.name: Contextual
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether this is a contextual tab. Contextual tabs, such as the Sketch tab in the Sketch environment, come and go based on the current environment. If a value of False is provided, the tab is added visibly. If a value of True is provided, the tab is added invisibly. Contextual tabs should then be added to the Environment.AdditionalVisibleRibbonTabs so that they show up visible in the appropriate environment(s).

member.name: M:Inventor.RibDefinition.Copy
member.summary:
Method that creates a copy of this RibDefinition object. The new RibDefinition object is independent of any feature. It can be edited and used as input to edit an existing feature or to create a new Rib feature. One typical use of this method is when you need to make several changes to an existing Rib feature. If you edit the RibDefinition object associated with the Rib feature, the feature will recompute after each edit. It’s more efficient to make a copy, edit the copy, and then assign the copy to the feature. This will result in a single recompute.
The RibFeatures.CreateDefinition method can also be used to create an independent RibDefinition object. The difference is that one created with the Copy method will have the same initial values as the object is was copied from. One that’s created with the CreateDefinition method will be initialized to predefined default values.

member.name: M:Inventor.RibFeatures.CreateDefinition(Inventor.ObjectCollection,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that creates a new RibDefinition object. The object created does not represent a rib feature but instead is a representation of the information that defines a rib feature. You can use this object as input to the RibFeatures.Add method to create the actual feature.

param.name: ProfileCurves
param.summary: Input ObjectCollection containing the sketch entities that will form the profile of the feature.

param.name: IsRib
param.summary: Input Boolean that specifies whether the sketch profile is projected lateral to the sketch plane (rib) or normal to the sketch plane (web) to create the feature. A value of True indicates that the profile is projected lateral to the sketch plane.

param.name: DirectionReversed
param.summary: Input Boolean that specifies whether the direction of the profile projection should be reversed. If the profile is projected normal to the sketch plane, setting this property to True causes the profile to be projected in the reverse direction of the sketch normal. If the profile is projected lateral to the sketch plane, setting this property to True causes the profile to be projected in the reverse direction of the natural normal direction of the base sketch entity. The natural normal of a sketch entity is defined as the cross-product of the vector representing the tangent at that point and the vector representing the sketch normal.

param.name: Thickness
param.summary: Input Variant that defines the thickness of the rib feature. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document.

param.summary: Output geometry object that helps to define the joint.

param.name: AdditionalInfo
param.summary: Output NameValueMap that contains additional information about the joint. This is used for some joints where the geometry information is not enough to completely define the joint. Also the name 'GearType' is passed back with a corresponding String indicating the type of gear; 'Rotational' or 'RackAndPinion'.

member.name: M:Inventor.RipDefinition.SetPointToPointRipType(Inventor.Face,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,Inventor.PartFeatureExtentDirectionEnum)
member.summary: Method that sets the RipDefinition so that it defines a point to point rip.

param.name: RipFace
param.summary: The face that the rip is defined along. This must be a face this is valid for defining a rip extent. For example a face along the edge of the part where the thickness of the part is represented is not valid as input.

param.name: PointOne
param.summary: Point that defines the location of the first rip point. Valid input includes Vertex, WorkPoint, SketchPoint, and SketchPoint3D objects.

param.name: PointTwo
param.summary: Point that defines the location of the second rip point. Valid input includes Vertex, WorkPoint, SketchPoint, and SketchPoint3D objects.

param.name: GapSize
param.summary: Variant that defines the width of the gap. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document.

param.name: GapSide
param.summary: Input PartFeatureExtentDirectionEnum value to indicate the position of the gap. Valid values are kPositiveExtentDirection, kNegativeExtentDirection, and kSymmetricExtentDirection. kPositiveExtentDirection indicates that the material will be removed from the right from the perspective of the first rip point where 'up' is along the normal of the rip face and you're looking towards the second rip point.

param.summary: The point that defines the location of the rip. Valid input includes Vertex, WorkPoint, SketchPoint, and SketchPoint3D objects.

param.name: GapSize
param.summary: Variant that defines the width of the gap. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document.

param.name: GapSide
param.summary: Input PartFeatureExtentDirectionEnum value to indicate the position of the gap. Valid values are kPositiveExtentDirection, kNegativeExtentDirection, and kSymmetricExtentDirection. kPositiveExtentDirection indicates that the material will be removed from the right from the perspective of the rip point where 'up' is along the normal of the rip face and you're looking towards the other edge of the face where the rip will end.

member.name: M:Inventor.RotateRotateConstraint.ConvertToAngleConstraint(System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,Inventor.AngleConstraintSolutionTypeEnum,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that converts the constraint to an angle constraint, and returns the AngleConstraint object. This method can also be used to edit the geometries associated with an angle constraint without changing its type, in which case the same object is returned by the method.

param.name: EntityOne
param.summary: Input object that defines the first object. This object can be a planar face, work plane, linear edge, work axis, or a face that defines an axis.

param.name: EntityTwo
param.summary: Input object that defines the second object. This object can be a planar face, work plane, linear edge, work axis, or a face that defines an axis.

param.name: Angle
param.summary: Input Variant that defines the angle between the two input entities. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value is created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are radians. If a string is input the units can be specified as part of the string or will default to the current angle units of the document.

param.name: SolutionType
param.summary: Optional input AngleConstraintSolutionTypeEnum that specifies the solution type. If specified to be kDirectedSolution, the solution always applies the right hand rule. If specified to be kUndirectedSolution, the solution allows either orientation, thus resolving situations where component orientation flips during a constraint drive or drag. If specified to be kReferenceVectorSolution, the ReferenceVectorEntity argument must be provided with a third entity for the solution. The default value is kDirectedSolution.

param.name: ReferenceVectorEntity
param.summary: Optional input object that provides a third entity to solve the angle constraint. This argument is ignored if the SolutionType argument is not kReferenceVectorSolution. This object can be a planar face, work plane, linear edge, work axis, or a face that defines an axis.

param.name: BiasPointOne
param.summary: Optional input Point object that is used help in determining the initial position of the occurrence. The occurrences are repositioned in an attempt to make the two bias points coincident. This provides some general control over the position of the occurrence when it isn't being controlled by another constraint. An example of when the bias points are useful is the case when the first constraint on a part is a mate constraint. In the case where the mate is between two planes, the parts can be positioned anywhere along the infinite plane that defines their mating contact. Using the bias points you can define the position of the two occurrences, relative to each other. If a bias point is not given, one is calculated that is at the center of the parameter range of the input entity.

param.name: BiasPointTwo
param.summary: Optional input Point object that is used help in determining the initial position of the occurrence. The occurrences are repositioned in an attempt to make the two bias points coincident. This provides some general control over the position of the occurrence when it isn't being controlled by another constraint. An example of when the bias points are useful is the case when the first constraint on a part is a mate constraint. param.name: EntityOneInferredType
param.summary: Optional input enum that specifies how the geometry of entity one is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity one, different options are possible. If entity one is a cylinder this can be either kNoInferrence or kInferredLine. For kNoInferrence to be valid for a cylinder, entity two must also be a cylinder and they must be the same radius. If entity one is a sphere this can be either kNoInferrence or kInferredPoint. For kNoInferrence to be valid for a sphere, entity two must also be a sphere and they must be the same radius. If entity one is a cone this can be either kNoInferrence or kInferredLine. For kNoInferrence to be valid for a cone, entity two must also be a cone and they must have the same taper angle. If entity one is a torus this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInferrence is valid.

param.name: EntityTwoInferredType
param.summary: Input enum that specifies how the geometry of entity two is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity two, different options are possible. If entity two is a torus this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInferrence is valid.

param.name: BiasPointOne
param.summary: Optional input Point object that is used help in determining the initial position of the occurrence. The occurrences are repositioned in an attempt to make the two bias points coincident. This provides some general control over the position of the occurrence when it isn't being controlled by another constraint. An example of when the bias points are useful is the case when the first constraint on a part is a mate constraint. In the case where the mate is between two planes, the parts can be positioned anywhere along the infinite plane that defines their mating contact. Using the bias points you can define the position of the two occurrences, relative to each other. If a bias point is not given, one is calculated that is at the center of the parameter range of the input entity.

member.summary: Converts the constraint to a symmetry constraint, and returns the AssemblySymmetryConstraint object.

param.name: EntityOne
param.summary: Input entity that is to be symmetric.

param.name: EntityTwo
param.summary: Input entity that is to be symmetric.

param.name: SymmetryPlane
param.summary: Input planar entity that defines the symmetry plane. This can either be a planar face or a work plane.

param.name: EntityOneInferredType
param.summary: Optional input constant that specifies how the geometry of entity one is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity one, different options are possible. If entity one is a linear entity this can be either kNoInference or kInferredPoint, for kInferredPoint the mid-point of the linear entity is used for the constraint. If entity one is a circular/elliptical sketch entity, this can be either kInferredPiont or kInferredLine. If entity one is a cylindrical, elliptic-cylindrical, conical face this can be kNoInference or kInferredLine. If entity one is a toroidal face this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. If entity one is a spherical face this can be kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInference is valid.

param.name: EntityTwoInferredType
param.summary: Optional input enum that specifies how the geometry of entity two is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity two, different options are possible. If entity two is a linear entity this can be either kNoInference or kInferredPoint, for kInferredPoint the mid-point of the linear entity is used for the constraint. If entity two is a circular/elliptical sketch entity, this can be either kInferredPiont or kInferredLine. If entity two is a cylindrical, elliptic-cylindrical, conical face this can be kNoInference or kInferredLine. If entity two is a toroidal face this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. If entity two is a spherical face this can be kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInference is valid.

param.name: NormalsOpposed
param.summary: This argument only applies when the two entities are planar (planar face or work plane) and defines if the normal of the planar entities are oriented so they are opposed or aligned. If the input entities are not planar, this argument is ignored. If they are planar and this argument is not specified they will defined to be opposed.

param.name: Offset
param.summary: Input Variant that defines the offset between the two input entities. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value is created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input the units can be specified as part of the string or will default to the current length units of the document.

param.name: BiasPointOne
param.summary: Optional input Point object that is used help in determining the initial position of the occurrence. The occurrences are repositioned in an attempt to make the two bias points coincident. This provides some general control over the position of the occurrence when it isn't being controlled by another constraint. An example of when the bias points are useful is the case when the first constraint on a part is a mate constraint. In the case where the mate is between two planes, the parts can be positioned anywhere along the infinite plane that defines their mating contact. Using the bias points you can define the position of the two occurrences, relative to each other. If a bias point is not given, one is calculated that is at the center of the parameter range of the input entity.

param.name: EntityOneInferredType
param.summary: Optional input enum that specifies how the geometry of entity one is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity one, different options are possible. If entity one is a cylinder this can be either kNoInferrence or kInferredLine. For kNoInferrence to be valid for a cylinder, entity two must also be a cylinder and they must be the same radius. If entity one is a sphere this can be either kNoInferrence or kInferredPoint. For kNoInferrence to be valid for a sphere, entity two must also be a sphere and they must be the same radius. If entity one is a cone this can be either kNoInferrence or kInferredLine. For kNoInferrence to be valid for a cone, entity two must also be a cone and they must have the same taper angle. If entity one is a torus this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInferrence is valid.

member.name: M:Inventor.RotateRotateConstraintProxy.ConvertToSymmetryConstraint(System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,Inventor.InferredTypeEnum,Inventor.InferredTypeEnum,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Converts the constraint to a symmetry constraint, and returns the AssemblySymmetryConstraint object.

param.name: EntityOne
param.summary: Input entity that is to be symmetric.

param.name: EntityTwo
param.summary: Input entity that is to be symmetric.

param.name: SymmetryPlane
param.summary: Input planar entity that defines the symmetry plane. This can either be a planar face or a work plane.

param.name: EntityOneInferredType
param.summary: Optional input constant that specifies how the geometry of entity one is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity one, different options are possible. If entity one is a linear entity this can be either kNoInference or kInferredPoint, for kInferredPoint the mid-point of the linear entity is used for the constraint. If entity one is a circular/elliptical sketch entity, this can be either kInferredPiont or kInferredLine. If entity one is a cylindrical, elliptic-cylindrical, conical face this can be kNoInference or kInferredLine. If entity one is a toroidal face this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. If entity one is a spherical face this can be kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInference is valid.

param.name: EntityTwoInferredType
param.summary: Optional input enum that specifies how the geometry of entity two is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity two, different options are possible. If entity two is a linear entity this can be either kNoInference or kInferredPoint, for kInferredPoint the mid-point of the linear entity is used for the constraint. If entity two is a circular/elliptical sketch entity, this can be either kInferredPiont or kInferredLine. If entity two is a cylindrical, elliptic-cylindrical, conical face this can be kNoInference or kInferredLine. If entity two is a toroidal face this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. If entity two is a spherical face this can be kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInference is valid.

param.name: NormalsOpposed
param.summary: This argument only applies when the two entities are planar (planar face or work plane) and defines if the normal of the planar entities are oriented so they are opposed or aligned. If the input entities are not planar, this argument is ignored. If they are planar and this argument is not specified they will defined to be opposed.

member.name: M:Inventor.RotateTranslateConstraint.ConvertToAngleConstraint(System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,Inventor.AngleConstraintSolutionTypeEnum,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that converts the constraint to an angle constraint, and returns the AngleConstraint object. This method can also be used to edit the geometries associated with an angle constraint without changing its type, in which case the same object is returned by the method.

param.name: EntityOne
param.summary: Input object that defines the first object. This object can be a planar face, work plane, linear edge, work axis, or a face that defines an axis.

param.name: EntityTwo
param.summary: Input object that defines the second object. This object can be a planar face, work plane, linear edge, work axis, or a face that defines an axis.

param.name: Angle
param.summary: Input Variant that defines the angle between the two input entities. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value is created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are radians. If a string is input the units can be specified as part of the string or will default to the current angle units of the document.

param.name: SolutionType
param.summary: Optional input AngleConstraintSolutionTypeEnum that specifies the solution type. If specified to be kDirectedSolution, the solution always applies the right hand rule. If specified to be kUndirectedSolution, the solution allows either orientation, thus resolving situations where component orientation flips during a constraint drive or drag. If specified to be kReferenceVectorSolution, the ReferenceVectorEntity argument must be provided with a third entity for the solution. The default value is kDirectedSolution.

param.name: ReferenceVectorEntity
param.summary: Optional input object that provides a third entity to solve the angle constraint. This argument is ignored if the SolutionType argument is not kReferenceVectorSolution. This object can be a planar face, work plane, linear edge, work axis, or a face that defines an axis.

param.name: BiasPointOne
param.summary: Optional input Point object that is used help in determining the initial position of the occurrence. The occurrences are repositioned in an attempt to make the two bias points coincident. This provides some general control over the position of the occurrence when it isn't being controlled by another constraint. An example of when the bias points are useful is the case when the first constraint on a part is a mate constraint. In the case where the mate is between two planes, the parts can be positioned anywhere along the infinite plane that defines their mating contact. Using the bias points you can define the position of the two occurrences, relative to each other. If a bias point is not given, one is calculated that is at the center of the parameter range of the input entity.

member.summary: Method that converts the constraint to a mate constraint, and returns the MateConstraint object. This method can also be used to edit the geometries associated with a mate constraint without changing its type, in which case the same object is returned by the method.

param.summary: Input Variant that defines the offset between the two input entities. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value is created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input the units can be specified as part of the string or will default to the current length units of the document.

param.name: EntityOneInferredType
param.summary: Optional input enum that specifies how the geometry of entity one is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity one, different options are possible. If entity one is a cylinder this can be either kNoInferrence or kInferredLine. For kNoInferrence to be valid for a cylinder, entity two must also be a cylinder and they must be the same radius. If entity one is a sphere this can be either kNoInferrence or kInferredPoint. For kNoInferrence to be valid for a sphere, entity two must also be a sphere and they must be the same radius. If entity one is a cone this can be either kNoInferrence or kInferredLine. For kNoInferrence to be valid for a cone, entity two must also be a cone and they must have the same taper angle. If entity one is a torus this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInferrence is valid.

param.name: EntityTwoInferredType

In the case where the mate is between two planes, the parts can be positioned anywhere along the infinite plane that defines their mating contact. Using the bias points you can define the position of the two occurrences, relative to each other. If a bias point is not given, one is calculated that is at the center of the parameter range of the input entity.

member.name: M:Inventor.RotateTranslateConstraint.ConvertToSymmetryConstraint(System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,Inventor.InferredTypeEnum,Inventor.InferredTypeEnum,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Converts the constraint to a symmetry constraint, and returns the AssemblySymmetryConstraint object.

param.name: EntityOne
param.summary: Input entity that is to be symmetric.

param.name: EntityTwo
param.summary: Input entity that is to be symmetric.

param.name: SymmetryPlane
param.summary: Input planar entity that defines the symmetry plane. This can either be a planar face or a work plane.

param.name: EntityOneInferredType
param.summary: Optional input constant that specifies how the geometry of entity one is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity one, different options are possible. If entity one is a linear entity this can be either kNoInference or kInferredPoint, for kInferredPoint the mid-point of the linear entity is used for the constraint. If entity one is a circular/elliptical sketch entity, this can be either kInferredPiont or kInferredLine. If entity one is a cylindrical, elliptic-cylindrical, conical face this can be kNoInference or kInferredLine. If entity one is a toroidal face this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. If entity one is a spherical face this can be kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInference is valid.

param.name: EntityTwoInferredType
param.summary: Optional input enum that specifies how the geometry of entity two is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity two, different options are possible. If entity two is a linear entity this can be either kNoInference or kInferredPoint, for kInferredPoint the mid-point of the linear entity is used for the constraint. If entity two is a circular/elliptical sketch entity, this can be either kInferredPiont or kInferredLine. If entity two is a cylindrical, elliptic-cylindrical, conical face this can be kNoInference or kInferredLine. If entity two is a toroidal face this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. If entity two is a spherical face this can be kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInference is valid.

param.name: NormalsOpposed
param.summary: This argument only applies when the two entities are planar (planar face or work plane) and defines if the normal of the planar entities are oriented so they are opposed or aligned. If the input entities are not planar, this argument is ignored. If they are planar and this argument is not specified they will defined to be opposed.

member.summary: Converts the constraint to a symmetry constraint, and returns the AssemblySymmetryConstraint object.

param.name: EntityOne
param.summary: Input entity that is to be symmetric.

param.name: EntityTwo
param.summary: Input entity that is to be symmetric.

param.name: SymmetryPlane
param.summary: Input planar entity that defines the symmetry plane. This can either be a planar face or a work plane.

param.name: EntityOneInferredType
param.summary: Optional input constant that specifies how the geometry of entity one is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity one, different options are possible. If entity one is a linear entity this can be either kNoInference or kInferredPoint, for kInferredPoint the mid-point of the linear entity is used for the constraint. If entity one is a circular/elliptical sketch entity, this can be either kInferredPiont or kInferredLine. If entity one is a cylindrical, elliptic-cylindrical, conical face this can be kNoInference or kInferredLine. If entity one is a toroidal face this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. If entity one is a spherical face this can be kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInference is valid.

param.name: EntityTwoInferredType
param.summary: Optional input enum that specifies how the geometry of entity two is to be interpreted. Depending on the geometry of the entity two, different options are possible. If entity two is a linear entity this can be either kNoInference or kInferredPoint, for kInferredPoint the mid-point of the linear entity is used for the constraint. If entity two is a circular/elliptical sketch entity, this can be either kInferredPiont or kInferredLine. If entity two is a cylindrical, elliptic-cylindrical, conical face this can be kNoInference or kInferredLine. If entity two is a toroidal face this can be either kInferredLine or kInferredPoint. If entity two is a spherical face this can be kInferredPoint. For a plane, only kNoInference is valid.

param.name: NormalsOpposed
param.summary: This argument only applies when the two entities are planar (planar face or work plane) and defines if the normal of the planar entities are oriented so they are opposed or aligned. If the input entities are not planar, this argument is ignored. If they are planar and this argument is not specified they will defined to be opposed.
