member.name: M:Inventor.SketchBlockDefinitionProxy.OffsetSketchEntitiesUsingDistance(Inventor.ObjectCollection,System.Double,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that offsets a sketch entity or a group of connected sketch entities. In both cases, the base sketch entity is first offset by the specified distance and along the specified direction. The base sketch entity is determined as follows: * If only one sketch entity needs to be offset, it will be treated as the base sketch entity. * If a group of end-to-end connected entities need to be offset, the first entity in the group will be treated as the base sketch entity. If this method successfully offsets the specified input sketch entities, the newly created sketch entities are returned.

param.name: SketchEntities
param.summary: ObjectCollection that specifies either a single sketch entity or a set of sketch entities that need to be offset. The collection can contain any SketchEntity object except SketchPoint because sketch points cannot be offset. The first entity in the collection is always treated as the base sketch entity. The offset distance (OffsetDistance argument) and the offset direction (NaturalOffsetDirection argument) apply to this base sketch entity. If only one sketch entity needs to be offset, then it should be specified as the only item in the collection and the IncludeConnectedEntities argument should be specified as False. Since the entity specified in the collection is the first and only item in the collection, it will be treated as the base sketch entity. If a group of end-to-end connected sketch entities need to be offset, then they can be specified using one of the following options: * Specifying an exact set of sketch entities to offset. The collection can be used to specify an exact set of sketch entities that need to be offset. The objects in the collection must represent entities that are end-to-end connected and the collection must contain the objects in the order that they are connected. The first entity specified in the collection will be treated as the base sketch entity. * Specifying only the base sketch entity and automatically including connected entities. The base sketch entity should be specified as the only item in the collection. The IncludeConnectedEntities boolean argument should be specified as True to indicate that all entities that form a loop (open or closed) which contains the base sketch entity should be automatically included to be offset. Since only one of the above options to specify a group of connected entities can be used at the same time and not both, if the collection contains multiple entities, it implies that the collection is being used to explicitly specify an exact set of sketch entities to offset, in which case the IncludeConnectedEntities argument should be False. If True is specified, the method will fail and the sketch entities will not be offset.

param.name: OffsetDistance
param.summary: Specifies the offset distance for the base sketch entity (the sketch entity specified by the first item in the SketchEntities collection). Since a group of connected entities that need to be offset will all be offset by the same distance, it implies that the distance value specified by this argument will be used not only for the base sketch entity but also for all the remaining connected sketch entities. Since the offset of the base sketch entity can lie on either side of the base entity, the offset distance in itself does not provide sufficient information regarding the final position for the offset of the base sketch entity. The NaturalOffsetDirection boolean argument can be used to specify one out of the two possible offset directions for the base sketch entity. Thus, the offset distance specified by this argument and the offset direction specified by the NaturalOffsetDirection boolean argument together determine the final position for the offset of the base sketch entity. Once the offset position for the base sketch entity is determined, the offset positions for any other additional connected sketch entities can be inferred.

param.name: NaturalOffsetDirection
param.summary: Value that can be used to specify one out of the two possible offset directions. This argument applies to the base sketch entity (the sketch entity specified by the first item in the SketchEntities collection). The natural offset direction is along the natural normal direction at any point on the base sketch entity which in-turn is defined as the cross-product of the vector representing the tangent at that point and the vector representing the sketch normal. If True is specified, then the points on the offset of the base sketch entity will be positioned in the direction specified by the natural normal at the corresponding points on the original base sketch entity. If False is specified, then the offset of the base sketch entity will be positioned in the direction opposite to that of the natural normal. Thus, this argument determines on which side of the base sketch entity the offset of the base sketch entity will be placed. Since this argument specifies only the offset direction, the OffsetDistance argument has to be used to specify the offset distance along the offset direction specified by this argument. Thus, the offset direction specified by this argument and the offset distance specified by the OffsetDistance argument together determine the final position for the offset of the base sketch entity. Once the offset position for the base sketch entity is determined, the offset positions for any other additional connected sketch entities can be inferred.

param.name: IncludeConnectedEntities
param.summary: Value that specifies whether all entities that form a loop containing the base sketch entity should also be offset. If True is specified, then all loop entities will be offset. But, if the sketch has multiple loops that contain the base sketch entity in which case it will not be possible to uniquely determine a single loop that needs to be offset, only the base sketch entity will be offset. If False is specified, then only the entities specified in the SketchEntities collection will be offset. If True is specified, the SketchEntities collection should contain only one item that corresponds to the base sketch entity, otherwise, if the SketchEntities collection contains multiple entities, then this method will fail and the sketch entities will not be offset. If False is specified, the SketchEntities collection can contain either a single item that corresponds to the base sketch entity or multiple items that correspond to a group of end-to-end connected entities. If the collection contains a single item that corresponds to the base sketch entity, then only this base sketch entity will be offset. On the other hand, if the collection contains multiple items, it implies that the collection is being used to specify an exact set of sketch entities to offset, hence, only those exact set of sketch entities will be offset. If no value is specified for this argument, then a default value of False will be assumed.

param.name: CreateOffsetConstraints
param.summary: Value that specifies whether offset constraints between the original and offset entities should be automatically created. If True is specified, then offset constraints will be automatically created. If False is specified, then offset constraints will not be created. If no value is specified, then a default value of True will be assumed to indicate that the offset constraints will be automatically created.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchBlockDefinitionProxy.OffsetSketchEntitiesUsingPoint(Inventor.ObjectCollection,Inventor.Point2d,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that offsets a sketch entity or a group of end-to-end connected sketch entities. In both cases, the offset is first applied to the base sketch entity such that the offset of the base sketch entity passes through the specified offset point on the sketch. The shortest distance of this offset point from the original base sketch entity determines the offset distance.

param.name: SketchEntities
param.summary: ObjectCollection that specifies either a single sketch entity or a set of sketch entities that need to be offset. The collection can contain any SketchEntity object except SketchPoint because sketch points cannot be offset. The first entity in the collection is always treated as the base sketch entity. The offset distance (OffsetDistance argument) and the offset direction (NaturalOffsetDirection argument) apply to this base sketch entity. If only one sketch entity needs to be offset, then it should be specified as the only item in the collection and the IncludeConnectedEntities argument should be specified as False. Since the entity specified in the collection is the first and only item in the collection, it will be treated as the base sketch entity. If a group of end\-to\-end connected sketch entities need to be offset, then they can be specified using one of the following options\: * Specifying an exact set of sketch entities to offset. The collection can be used to specify an exact set of sketch entities that need to be offset. The objects in the collection must represent entities that are end-to-end connected and the collection must contain the objects in the order that they are connected. The first entity specified in the collection will be treated as the base sketch entity. * Specifying only the base sketch entity and automatically including connected entities. The base sketch entity should be specified as the only item in the collection. The IncludeConnectedEntities boolean argument should be specified as True to indicate that all entities that form a loop (open or closed) which contains the base sketch entity should be automatically included to be offset. Since only one of the above options to specify a group of connected entities can be used at the same time and not both, if the collection contains multiple entities, it implies that the collection is being used to explicitly specify an exact set of sketch entities to offset, in which case the IncludeConnectedEntities argument should be False. If True is specified, the method will fail and the sketch entities will not be offset.

param.name: OffsetPoint
param.summary: Defines a point on the sketch through which the offset of the base sketch entity (the sketch entity specified by the first item in the SketchEntities collection) should pass. The shortest distance of this point from the base sketch entity is used to determine the offset distance. This offset distance will also be used to offset any other additional connected sketch entities. The location of the point with respect to the base sketch entity determines the position of the offset base sketch entity (i.e. the location of the point determines on which side of the base sketch entity the offset of the base sketch entity will be positioned). Once the offset distance and position for the offset of the base sketch entity are determined, this information is used to determine the position for all other connected sketch entities that need to be offset. Thus, the offset point provides sufficient information to calculate the offset distance as well as the offset direction for all the sketch entities that need to be offset.

param.name: IncludeConnectedEntities
param.summary: Value that specifies whether all entities that form a loop containing the base sketch entity should also be offset. If True is specified, then all loop entities will be offset. But, if the sketch has multiple loops that contain the base sketch entity in which case it will not be possible to uniquely determine a single loop that needs to be offset, only the base sketch entity will be offset. If False is specified, then only the entities specified in the SketchEntities collection will be offset. If True is specified, the SketchEntities collection should contain only one item that corresponds to the base sketch entity, otherwise, if the SketchEntities collection contains multiple entities, then this method will fail and the sketch entities will not be offset. If False is specified, the SketchEntities collection can contain either a single item that corresponds to the base sketch entity or multiple items that correspond to a group of end\-to\-end connected entities. If the collection contains a single item that corresponds to the base sketch entity, then only this base sketch entity will be offset. On the other hand, if the collection contains multiple items, it implies that the collection is being used to specify an exact set of sketch entities to offset, hence, only those exact set of sketch entities will be offset. If no value is specified for this argument, then a default value of False will be assumed.

param.name: CreateOffsetConstraints
param.summary: Value that specifies whether offset constraints between the original and offset entities should be automatically created. If True is specified, then offset constraints will be automatically created. If False is specified, then offset constraints will not be created. If no value is specified, then a default value of True will be assumed to indicate that the offset constraints will be automatically created.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchBlockDefinitionProxy.RotateSketchObjects(Inventor.ObjectCollection,Inventor.Point2d,System.Double,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that rotates a collection of sketch objects by a specified angle. If the Copy argument is set to True, the newly created objects are returned.

param.name: SketchObjects
param.summary: Input ObjectCollection that contains the sketch elements to rotate. The collection must contain at least one object and can be any SketchEntity, a TextBox or an Image.

param.name: CenterPoint
param.summary: Input Point2d object that defines the center point to rotate the elements about.

param.name: Angle
param.summary: Input Double that defines the angle to rotate the elements by in radians.

param.name: Copy
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether to copy the sketch elements to the new location or to rotate them. If not specified, a default value of False is used indicating that the elements will be rotated.

param.name: RemoveConstraints
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether to remove or retain some of the constraints that constrain the input sketch entities to other geometry. If not specified, a default value of False is used indicating that the constraints will be retained.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchBlockDefinitionProxy.SetEndOfPart(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that repositions the end-of-part marker relative to the object this method is called from. The argument defines if the end-of-part marker will be positioned just before or just after the object. If the object is contained within another object and is not in the top level of the browser, the positioning of the marker will be relative to the top-level object the calling object is contained within. An example of this case is a sketch that has not been shared and has been consumed by a feature. Another example is a nested work feature.

param.name: Before
param.summary: Input Boolean that indicates if the end of part marker should be immediately before or after this work feature. A value of True indicates before and False indicates after.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchCircle3D.ReferencedEntity
member.summary: Property that returns the object this entity is dependent on. When sketch entities are created by projecting model edges or intersecting the model, the resulting entities are driven by the original model entities and cannot be modified. This property returns the model entity the sketch entity is dependent on. The Reference property indicates whether the sketch entity is driven by a model entity or not. If the sketch entity is not referencing a model entity, this property will return Nothing. This property can also return nothing even when the sketch entity is referencing a model entity in the case where the model entity has been consumed by some subsequent modeling operation.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchCircularPatterns.CreateDefinition(Inventor.ObjectCollection,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Creates a new sketch circular pattern definition. The new SketchCircularPatternDefinition object is returned.

param.name: Geometries
param.summary: Input ObjectCollection object that contains the sketch geometries to be patterned. The collection could contain the various sketch entities and sketch blocks. When a SketchEntity has containing SketchBlock the SketchBlock should be used as input. The TextBox can’t be included in this argument but it can be included in a containing SketchBlock.

param.name: AxisEntity
param.summary: Input sketch entity that defines the axis entity. This can be a SketchPoint, SketchArc or SketchCircle.

param.name: NaturalAxisDirection
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that indicates if the direction of the pattern is in the natural direction of the AxisEntity or reversed. A value of True indicates it is in the natural direction. If not provided this default to True.

param.name: Count
param.summary: Optional input Variant that defines the number of instances in the x direction. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter will be created to control this value when the pattern is created. If a string is input it can be any string that can be evaluated by Inventor to result in a unitless number(e.g. the name of a unitless Parameter).

param.name: Angle
param.summary: Optional input String or value to specify the angle between instances. A parameter will be created to control angle between instances when the pattern is created. If a value is input, the units are radians. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current angle units of the document, or it can be a name of an angular parameter.

param.name: Symmetric
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether the occurrences are distributed on both sides of the original geometry. A value of True indicates the occurrences are distributed on both sides of the original geometry. If not provided this defaults to False.

param.name: Associative
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether the pattern will update when changes are made to the part. If set this to False then the pattern constraints will be removed and the pattern will not update when change an element. If not provided this defaults to True.

param.name: Fitted
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether pattern elements are equally fitted within the specified angle. If set to False, the pattern spacing measures the distance between elements instead of the overall angle for the pattern. If not provided this defaults to True.

param.name: SuppressedElements
param.summary: Optional input Long array that specifies the indices of the elements to be suppressed.

param.name: Reserved
param.summary: Reserved for future use.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.Constraints
member.summary: Property that returns a collection of sketch constraints that are tied directly to this entity. This collection consists of both geometric and dimension constraints.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.ConstraintStatus
member.summary: Read-only property that returns the constraint status of the sketch. Possible return values are kFullyConstrainedConstraintStatus, kOverConstrainedConstraintStatus, kUnderConstrainedConstraintStatus, and kUnknownConstraintStatus.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.Construction
member.summary: Gets and sets whether the entity behaves as a construction entity or not.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.ContainingSketchBlock
member.summary: Property that returns the sketch block that contains this object. This is the same SketchBlock returned as the last item in the SketchBlockPath property. This property returns Nothing if this object does not belong to a sketch block and lives directly under a sketch.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.ControlPoint
member.summary: Read-only property that returns the SketchPoint at the specified index. The indices correspond to the control points in order from the start to the end of the spline. An Index of 1 returns the first SketchPoint. The ControlPointCount property returns the total number of control points for the spline. Deleting the returned sketch point will delete the control point from the spline.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.ControlPointCount
member.summary: Read-only property that returns the number of control points defining the control point spline.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.ControlPolygonSide
member.summary: Read-only property that returns the SketchLine that represents a side of the control polygon. The indices correspond to the control polygon edges in order from the start to the end of the spline. An Index of 1 returns the first edge, with the last side being ControlPointCount -1 since there is one less side than number of control points.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.ConvertToSpline
member.summary: Method that inserts a new control point into the existing control point spline.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.CurvatureDisplay
member.summary: Specifies whether curvature information is displayed for the spline.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.Delete
member.summary: Method that deletes the sketch entity. This method will fail in the case where this object was created as a result of a derived part. The HasReferenceComponent property can be used to determine when this is the case.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.DisabledActionTypes
member.summary: Gets and sets whether specific user actions are blocked on this sketch geometry.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.EndSketchPoint
member.summary: Read-only property that returns the sketch point that defines the position of the end of the spline.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.Geometry
member.summary: Read-only property that returns a BSplineCurve2d geometry object. The object returned represents a 'snapshot' view of the current state of the spline.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.Geometry3d
member.summary: Read-only property that returns b-spline geometry that represents this spline in model space.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.GetCustomLineType(System.String@,System.String@)
member.summary: Method that returns information regarding the custom line type in use. The method returns a failure if the return value of the LineType property is not kCustomLineType.

param.name: LineTypeName
param.summary: Output string that returns the name of the line type.

param.name: LineTypeDescription
param.summary: Output string that returns the description of the line type.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.GetReferenceKey(System.Byte[]@,System.Int32)
member.summary: Method that generates and returns the reference key for this entity.

param.name: ReferenceKey
param.summary: Input/output array of Bytes that contains the reference key.

param.name: KeyContext
param.summary: Input Long that specifies the key context. The key context must be supplied when working with any B-Rep entities (and SurfaceBody, FaceShell, Face, Edge, EdgeUse and Vertex objects). A key context is created using the CreateKeyContext method of the ReferenceKeyManager object. For all other object types, the key context argument is not used and is ignored if provided.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.HasReferenceComponent
member.summary: Property that specifies if the object was created as the result of a derived part.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.InsertKnot(System.Double)
member.summary: Method that inserts a knot into the existing control point spline. The effect of this will be that the shape of the curve is maintained, but the control polygon will change shape and one additional point will be added.

param.name: Position
param.summary: The parametric position along the curve to insert the new knot.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.IsClosed
member.summary: Read-only property that returns whether the curve is closed.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.SetCustomLineType(System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that sets a custom line type to the curve from the specified .lin file. The method automatically changes the value of LineType property to kCustomLineType.

param.name: FullFileName
param.summary: Input string that specifies the full file name of the *.lin file containing the custom line types.

param.name: LineTypeName
param.summary: OInput string that specifies the name of the line type.

param.name: ReplaceExisting
param.summary: Input Boolean that specifies whether to replace the existing line type if a line type of the same name exists. If set to False, and a line type of the same name exists, this method returns an error.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline.SketchBlockPath
member.summary: Property that returns the path of sketch blocks at the leaf of which this sketch object is found. The enumerator returns a count of 0 if the object lives directly under a sketch.

member.name: T:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline3D
member.summary: The SketchControlPointSpline3D object represents a control point spline within a 3D sketch. These splines are created by defining the vertices of a control polygon of a NURBS curve. The properties and methods listed below are in addition to those supported by the SketchEntity3D object.

member.summary: Property that returns the ReferenceComponent that resulted in the creation of this feature.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchControlPointSpline3D.ReferencedEntity
member.summary: Property that returns the object this entity is dependent on. When sketch entities are created by projecting model edges or intersecting the model, the resulting entities are driven by the original model entities and cannot be modified. This property returns the model entity the sketch entity is dependent on. The Reference property indicates whether the sketch entity is driven by a model entity or not. If the sketch entity is not referencing a model entity, this property will return Nothing. This property can also return nothing even when the sketch entity is referencing a model entity in the case where the model entity has been consumed by some subsequent modeling operation.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchedSymbolDefinition.ExitEdit(System.Boolean,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that closes the currently active sketch (see below for limitations) and depending on the input parameters, replaces the sketch of the sketched symbol definition with the edited sketch.

param.name: SaveChanges
param.summary: Input Boolean that specifies whether to save the changes or not. True indicates to save the changes. Setting this property to False will cause the sketch to close and lose all edits.

param.name: SaveAsName
param.summary: Input String that specifies the name of the new sketched symbol definition to create. This argument is used in the case where the SaveChanges argument is True. If not specified, or an empty string is supplied, the edited sketch replaces the sketch associated with the sketched symbol definition being edited. If a string is supplied, a new sketched symbol definition is created and the edited sketch is used for it. The supplied name must be unique with respect to all other SketchedSymbolDefinition objects in the document.

member.name: T:Inventor.SketchedSymbols
member.summary: The SketchedSymbols collection object provides access to the objects on a specific sheet. It also provides the ability to place sketched symbols onto a sheet. See the article in the overviews section.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchedSymbols.Add(System.Object,Inventor.Point2d,System.Double,System.Double,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that places a sketched symbol onto the sheet.

param.name: SketchedSymbolDefinition
param.summary: Input Variant that specifies which SketchedSymbolDefinition to use. The input for the argument can be either a SketchedSymbolDefinition object or string containing the name of an existing SketchedSymbolDefinition object.

param.name: Position
param.summary: Input that specifies the location on the sheet to place the sketched symbol instance.

param.name: Rotation
param.summary: The rotation of the symbol, in radians.

param.name: Scale
param.summary: The scale of the symbol.

param.name: PromptStrings
param.summary: Optional input array of Strings that specifies the input strings to use as input for prompted text fields that my be present in the sketched symbol definition. If prompted strings exist in the sketched symbol definition you must supply input strings through this argument or this method will fail. The prompt strings and their order are obtained by querying the TextBox objects in the SketchedSymbolDefinition. The order they're returned by the TextBoxes collection is the same order the input strings need to be supplied in the PromptStrings array.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchedSymbols.AddWithLeader(System.Object,Inventor.ObjectCollection,System.Double,System.Double,System.Object,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that places a sketched symbol with a leader.

param.name: SketchedSymbolDefinition
param.summary: Input Variant that specifies which SketchedSymbolDefinition to use. The input for the argument can be either a SketchedSymbolDefinition object or string containing the name of an existing SketchedSymbolDefinition object.

param.name: LeaderPoints
param.summary: Input ObjectCollection containing a series of Point2d objects representing the leader originating at the symbol. The last item in the collection (even if it is the only item) can be a GeometryIntent object indicating a geometry to attach the leader to. A GeometryIntent object can be created using the Sheet.CreateGeometryIntent method. The ObjectCollection must contain at least one item, else the method will fail.

param.name: Rotation
param.summary: Optional input double that specifies a rotation angle for the symbol in radians. If not specified, a default value of 0 is used, indicating that no rotation is applied.

param.name: Scale
param.summary: Optional input double that specifies a scale for the symbol in radians. If not specified, a default value of 1 is used, indicating that no scaling is applied.

param.name: PromptStrings
param.summary: Optional input array of Strings that specifies the input strings to use as input for prompted text fields that my be present in the sketched symbol definition. If prompted strings exist in the sketched symbol definition you must supply input strings through this argument or this method will fail. The prompt strings and their order are obtained by querying the TextBox objects in the SketchedSymbolDefinition. The order they’re returned by the TextBoxes collection is the same order the input strings need to be supplied in the PromptStrings array.

param.name: SymbolClipping
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that indicates whether to trim the annotations applied to the symbol. If True, the annotations are trimmed. If not specified, a value of True is used.

param.name: Static
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that indicates whether to show the scale and rotation grip points on the symbol. If True, the grip points are disabled. If not specified, a value of False is used.

When sketch entities are created by projecting model edges or intersecting the model, the resulting entities are driven by the original model entities and cannot be modified. If the sketch entity is not referencing a model entity, this property will return Nothing. This property can also return nothing even when the sketch entity is referencing a model entity in the case where the model entity has been consumed by some subsequent modeling operation.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchEllipticalArc3DProxy.ReferencedEntity
member.summary: Property that returns the object this entity is dependent on. When sketch entities are created by projecting model edges or intersecting the model, the resulting entities are driven by the original model entities and cannot be modified. This property returns the model entity the sketch entity is dependent on. The Reference property indicates whether the sketch entity is driven by a model entity or not. If the sketch entity is not referencing a model entity, this property will return Nothing. This property can also return nothing even when the sketch entity is referencing a model entity in the case where the model entity has been consumed by some subsequent modeling operation.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchEvents.OnDelete(Inventor.Document,System.Object,Inventor.EventTimingEnum,Inventor.NameValueMap,Inventor.HandlingCodeEnum@)
member.summary: The OnDelete event notifies the client when a 2d or 3d sketch is being deleted. This notification is not sent when the contents of the sketch is deleted, but only when the sketch itself is deleted.

param.name: DocumentObject
param.summary: The Document object that contains the sketch.

param.name: Entity
param.summary: The sketch that is being deleted. When the value of the BeforeOrAfter argument is kBefore, the entity provided is the sketch before being deleted. When the value is kAfter, an object is also provided but since the actual entity has been deleted calling any methods or properties on the object will fail. The only thing that is valid to do with the object at this time is to compare it's identity with a reference previously saved. For example: Private m_oDeletedSketch As Object Private Sub oSketchEvents_OnDelete( ByVal DocumentObject As Document, ByVal Entity As Object, ByVal BeforeOrAfter As EventTimingEnum, ...) If BeforeOrAfter = kBefore Then ' Somehow Check to see if the sketch being deleted is an interesting one. ' For example, it could have an attribute attached to it to identify it. If Interesting(Entity) Then ' Save a reference to the object. Set m_ oDeletedSketch = Entity End If Else ' Now we're either after the delete or it's been aborted. ' Check to see if the sketch is the interesting one. If Entity is m_ oDeletedSketch Then If BeforeOrAfter = kAfter then ' The sketch was deleted. ElseIf BeforeOrAfter = kAbort Then ' The delete was aborted. End If End If End Sub

param.name: BeforeOrAfter
param.summary: Input EventTimingEnum indicating when the event is being fired. Notification is sent before and after the sketch is deleted.

param.name: Context
param.summary: Input NameValueMap object that can be used to determine the context of why the event fired. No context information is provided for this event.

param.name: HandlingCode
param.summary: Output HandlingCodeEnum that indicates how you are handling the event. The value of this argument is currently ignored for this event.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchLine3D.ReferencedEntity
member.summary: Property that returns the object this entity is dependent on. When sketch entities are created by projecting model edges or intersecting the model, the resulting entities are driven by the original model entities and cannot be modified. This property returns the model entity the sketch entity is dependent on. The Reference property indicates whether the sketch entity is driven by a model entity or not. If the sketch entity is not referencing a model entity, this property will return Nothing. This property can also return nothing even when the sketch entity is referencing a model entity in the case where the model entity has been consumed by some subsequent modeling operation.

member.name: T:Inventor.SketchLines
member.summary: The SketchLines object provides access to all of the objects in a sketch and provides methods to create additional sketch lines. See the article in the overviews section.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchLines.AddAsPolygon(System.Int32,System.Object,System.Object,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that creates a polygon with up to 120 sides. The sketch lines representing the polygon are returned.

param.name: NumberOfSides
param.summary: Input Long that specifies the number of sides of the polygon. If a value lesser than 3 or greater than 120 is provided, the method returns an error.

param.name: CenterPoint
param.summary: Input object that specifies the center of the polygon. This can either be a SketchPoint or a Point2d object.

param.name: CircumferencePoint
param.summary: Input object that specifies a point on the circumference of the circle that inscribes or circumscribes the polygon. This can either be a SketchPoint or a Point2d object.

param.name: Inscribed
param.summary: Input Boolean that specifies whether the specified CircumferencePoint is on a circle that inscribes or circumscribes the polygon.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchLines.AddAsThreePointCenteredRectangle(System.Object,System.Object,Inventor.Point2d)
member.summary: Method that creates four lines to represent a rectangle where the center of the rectangle is defined by a point, the length and orientation is defined by a second point, and the width defined by a third point.

param.name: CenterPoint
param.summary: Input object that specifies the center of the rectangle. This can either be a SketchPoint or a Point2d object.

param.name: EdgePoint
param.summary: Input object that specifies a point on the edge of the rectangle that defines the orientation and length of the rectangle.

param.name: WidthPoint
param.summary: Input Point2d that defines the width of the rectangle.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchLines.AddAsThreePointRectangle(System.Object,System.Object,Inventor.Point2d)
member.summary: Method that creates four lines to represent a rectangle where the base of the rectangle is defined by two points and the height is defined by a third point. The input points for the base can be either Point2d objects defining an X-Y point in space, or an existing SketchPoint object.

param.name: BasePointOne
param.summary: Input object that defines the first base point of the rectangle. Either a SketchPoint or Point2d object can be used. If an existing sketch point is input, that lines become connected to the point.

param.name: BasePointTwo
param.summary: Input object that defines the second base point of the rectangle. Either a SketchPoint or Point2d object can be used. If an existing sketch point is input, the lines become connected to the point.

param.name: HeightPoint
param.summary: Input Point2d object that defines the height of the rectangle. The point can be anywhere in space and the height of the rectangle is computed by finding the shortest distance of this point to an infinite line defined by the two base points.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchLines.AddAsTwoPointCenteredRectangle(System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that creates four lines to represent a rectangle where the center of the rectangle is defined by a point and the corner of the rectangle is defined by the second point and the rectangle is aligned with the sketch x and y axes. The input points can be either Point2d objects defining an x-y point in space, or an existing SketchPoint object. If an existing sketch point is input, the lines will become connected to that point. The created sketch lines are returned in a SketchEntitiesEnumerator object. This includes the four lines representing the rectangle and the two internal construction lines.

param.name: CenterPoint
param.summary: Input object that specifies the center of the rectangle. This can either be a SketchPoint or a Point2d object.

param.name: CornerPoint
param.summary: Input object that specifies a corner of the rectangle. This can either be a SketchPoint or a Point2d object.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchLines.AddAsTwoPointRectangle(System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that creates four lines to represent a rectangle where the diagonal corners of the rectangle are defined by the two input points and the rectangle is aligned with the sketch X and Y axes. The four new sketch lines are returned in an SketchEntitiesEnumerator object.

param.name: CornerPointOne
param.summary: Input object that defines a corner of the rectangle. This can be a SketchPoint or a Point2d object. If an existing sketch point is input, the lines become connected to that point and the point becomes the corner point of the rectangle.

param.name: CornerPointTwo
param.summary: Input object that defines the diagonal corner of the rectangle. This can be a SketchPoint or a Point2d object. If an existing sketch point is input, the lines become connected to that point and the point becomes the corner point of the rectangle.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchLines.AddByMidEndPoints(System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that creates a new sketch line based on the mid and end points. The new sketch line is returned.

param.name: MidPoint
param.summary: Input object that defines the mid point of the line. This can be either a Point2d object defining an x-y point in space, or an existing SketchPoint object. If an existing sketch point is input, a MidpointContraint will be created between the SketchPoint and the new sketch line.

param.name: EndPoint
param.summary: Input object that defines the end point of the line. This can be either a Point2d object defining an x-y point in space, or an existing SketchPoint object. If an existing sketch point is input, that point becomes the line’s end point.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchLines.AddByTwoPoints(System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that creates a new sketch line based on the two input points. The new sketch line is returned.

param.name: StartPoint
param.summary: Input object that defines the start point of the line. This can be either a Point2d object defining an x-y point in space, or an existing SketchPoint object. If an existing sketch point is input, that point becomes the line's start point.

param.name: EndPoint
param.summary: Input object that defines the end point of the line. This can be either a Point2d object defining an x-y point in space, or an existing SketchPoint object. If an existing sketch point is input, that point becomes the line's end point.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchLines.Application
member.summary: Returns the top-level parent application object. When used the context of Inventor, an Application object is returned. When used in the context of Apprentice, an ApprenticeServer object is returned.

member.summary: Property that returns the number of items in this collection.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchLines.Item
member.summary: Returns the specified SketchLine object from the collection.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchLines.Type
member.summary: Returns an ObjectTypeEnum indicating this object's type.

member.name: T:Inventor.SketchLines3D
member.summary: The SketchLines3D object provides access to all of the objects in a sketch and provides methods to create additional sketch lines. See the article in the overviews section.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchLines3D.AddByTwoPoints(System.Object,System.Object,System.Boolean,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that creates a new sketch line based on the two input points. The new sketch line is returned.

param.name: StartPoint
param.summary: Input object that defines the start point of the line. This can be either a vertex object, a workpoint, a SketchPoint, or an existing SketchPoint3D object. If an existing sketch point is input, that point becomes the line's start point.

param.name: EndPoint
param.summary: Input object that defines the end point of the line. This can be either a vertex object, a workpoint, a SketchPoint, or an existing SketchPoint3D object. If an existing sketch point is input, that point becomes the line's end point.

param.name: UseAutoBend
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that indicates whether a bend should be automatically applied if the StartPoint or the EndPoint is shared by another sketch line. The default is True, which means that the bend will be automatically applied.

param.name: BendRadius
param.summary: Optional input variant that defines the radius of the auto-bend. If the UseAutoBend flag is set to true and this variant is not supplied, a default value is used for the bend radius. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchOffsetSpline.Closed
member.summary: Boolean property that gets whether the curve is closed. A periodic curve is closed and curvature continuous at the closure.

member.summary: Property that returns a collection of sketch constraints that are tied directly to this entity. This collection consists of both geometric and dimension constraints.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchOffsetSpline.ConstraintStatus
member.summary: Read-only property that returns the constraint status of the sketch. Possible return values are kFullyConstrainedConstraintStatus, kOverConstrainedConstraintStatus, kUnderConstrainedConstraintStatus, and kUnknownConstraintStatus.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchOffsetSpline.Construction
member.summary: Gets and sets whether the entity behaves as a construction entity or not.

member.summary: Property that returns the sketch block that contains this object. This is the same SketchBlock returned as the last item in the SketchBlockPath property. This property returns Nothing if this object does not belong to a sketch block and lives directly under a sketch.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchPoint.MoveBy(Inventor.Vector2d)
member.summary: Method that moves the sketch point a delta distance from its current location. Movement of a sketch point is limited by the constraints currently defined on the sketch. If a sketch is partially constrained it will perform the move within the range allowed by the constraints. Because of this, the result of a move may not always be exactly what was specified.

param.name: Vector
param.summary: Input Vector2d object that defines the delta distance to move the sketch point.

param.name: Point
param.summary: Input object that defines the new position of the sketch point.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchPoint3D.ReferencedEntity
member.summary: Property that returns the object this entity is dependent on. When sketch entities are created by projecting model edges or intersecting the model, the resulting entities are driven by the original model entities and cannot be modified. This property returns the model entity the sketch entity is dependent on. The Reference property indicates whether the sketch entity is driven by a model entity or not. If the sketch entity is not referencing a model entity, this property will return Nothing. This property can also return nothing even when the sketch entity is referencing a model entity in the case where the model entity has been consumed by some subsequent modeling operation.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchRectangularPatterns.CreateDefinition(Inventor.ObjectCollection,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Creates a new sketch rectangular pattern definition. The new SketchRectangularPatternDefinition object is returned.

param.name: Geometries
param.summary: Input ObjectCollection object that contains the sketch geometries to be patterned. The collection could contain the various sketch entities and sketch blocks. When a SketchEntity has containing SketchBlock the SketchBlock should be used as input. The TextBox can’t be included in this argument but it can be included in a containing SketchBlock.

param.name: XDirectionEntity
param.summary: Input linear sketch entity that defines the X direction.

param.name: XCount
param.summary: Input Variant that defines the number of instances in the x direction. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter will be created to control this value when the pattern is created. If a string is input it can be any string that can be evaluated by Inventor to result in a unitless number(e.g. the name of a unitless Parameter).

param.name: NaturalXDirection
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that indicates if the direction of the pattern is in the natural direction of the XDirectionEntity or reversed. A value of True indicates it is in the natural direction. If not provided this default to True.

param.name: XDirectionSymmetric
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that indicates if the occurrences are distributed on both sides of the original geometry. If the occurrence count is even, NaturalXDirection can indicate which side gets the extra occurrence. A value of True indicates the occurrences are distributed on both sides of the original geometry. If not provided this default to False.

param.name: XSpacing
param.summary: Optional input String or value to specify the spacing between instances in the X direction. A parameter will be created to control spacing between instances in the X direction when the pattern is created. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document.

param.name: YDirectionEntity
param.summary: Optional input linear sketch entity that defines the Y direction.

param.name: YCount
param.summary: Optional input Variant that defines the number of instances in the Y direction. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter will be created to control this value when the pattern is created. If a string is input it can be any string that can be evaluated by Inventor to result in a unitless number(e.g. the name of a unitless Parameter).

param.name: NaturalYDirection
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that indicates if the direction of the pattern is in the natural direction of the YDirectionEntity or reversed. A value of True indicates it is in the natural direction. If not provided this default to True.

param.name: YDirectionSymmetric
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that indicates if the occurrences are distributed on both sides of the original geometry. If the occurrence count is even, NaturalYDirection can indicate which side gets the extra occurrence. A value of True indicates the occurrences are distributed on both sides of the original geometry. If not provided this default to False.

param.name: YSpacing
param.summary: Optional input String or value to specify the spacing between instances in the Y direction. A parameter will be created to control spacing between instances in the Y direction when the pattern is created. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document.

param.name: Associative
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether the pattern will update when changes are made to the part. If set this to False then the pattern constraints will be removed and the pattern will not update when change an element. If not provided this default to True.

param.name: Fitted
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether pattern elements are equally fitted within the specified distances. If set to False, the pattern spacing measures the distance between elements instead of the overall distance for the pattern. If not provided this default to False.

param.name: SuppressedElements
param.summary: Optional input Long array that specifies the indices of the elements to be suppressed.

param.name: Reserved
param.summary: Reserved for future use.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchSpline3D.InsertFitPoint(System.Object,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Method that inserts a new fit point into the spline and returns the inserted fit point.

param.name: FitPoint
param.summary: Input object that specifies the position of the new fit point. This can be a , a SketchPoint, a workpoint or a vertex. If the input is not a SketchPoint3D object, a SketchPoint3D object is automatically created at the position of the input point.

param.name: TargetIndex
param.summary: Optional input Long that specifies the existing fit point to insert the new fit point next to. If not supplied, this value defaults to 0. If the value is 0, then the new fit point is inserted between the two existing fit points that are closest to the new fit point.

param.name: InsertBefore
param.summary: Optional input Boolean indicating if the fit point should be inserted before or after the target index. The default is true, meaning that the new fit point will be inserted before the target index. This Boolean is ignored if the TargetIndex specified is 0.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchSpline3D.ReferencedEntity
member.summary: Property that returns the object this entity is dependent on. When sketch entities are created by projecting model edges or intersecting the model, the resulting entities are driven by the original model entities and cannot be modified. This property returns the model entity the sketch entity is dependent on. The Reference property indicates whether the sketch entity is driven by a model entity or not. If the sketch entity is not referencing a model entity, this property will return Nothing. This property can also return nothing even when the sketch entity is referencing a model entity in the case where the model entity has been consumed by some subsequent modeling operation.

member.name: M:Inventor.SketchSpline3D.Split(System.Object)
member.summary: Method that splits the spline at the specified location. After the split, the original object (the one on which this method was called) represents the part of the spline associated with the original start point. The SketchSpline3D object returned by this method represents the part of the spline associated with the original end point. The curvature of the final result may differ from the original spline.

param.name: FitPoint
param.summary: Input Variant value that specifies the location at which to split the spline. This can be either a numeric value indicating the index of the fit point (the indices corresponding to the fit points in order from the start to the end of the spline, where the first fit point has an index of 1) or it can be an existing fit point.

member.name: P:Inventor.SketchSplineHandle3DProxy.ReferencedEntity
member.summary: Property that returns the object this entity is dependent on. When sketch entities are created by projecting model edges or intersecting the model, the resulting entities are driven by the original model entities and cannot be modified. This property returns the model entity the sketch entity is dependent on. The Reference property indicates whether the sketch entity is driven by a model entity or not. If the sketch entity is not referencing a model entity, this property will return Nothing. This property can also return nothing even when the sketch entity is referencing a model entity in the case where the model entity has been consumed by some subsequent modeling operation.

member.name: M:Inventor.SlotDefinition.SetDistanceExtent(System.Object,Inventor.PartFeatureExtentDirectionEnum,System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that changes the extents to be Distance extents.

param.name: Distance
param.summary: Input Variant that specifies the depth to which to extend the slot feature. This can be either a numeric value or a string. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document.

param.name: ExtentDirection
param.summary: Input PartFeatureExtentDirectionEnum that indicates which side to extrude towards. Valid input is kPositiveExtentDirection or kNegativeExtentDirection. kPositiveExtentDirection defines the offset direction to be in the same direction as the normal of the sketch plane or direction of the geometry that defines the slot direction.

param.name: EndMillType
param.summary:
Optional input SlotEndMillTypeEnum that specifies the end mill type of the Slot. Valid value is kFlatEndMillType or kAngledEndMillType. If kAngledEndMillType is specified then the BottomTipAngle argument needs to be provided to specify the angle.
The default value is kFlatEndMillType .

param.name: BottomTipAngle
param.summary:
Optional input Variant that defines the angle of the tip at the bottom of a Slot. This argument is only used when the EndMillType argument is kAngledEndMillType. If this argument is not supplied a default value of 118 degrees is assigned.

param.summary: Input ObjectCollection containing sketch point(s) that defines the centerpoint(s) of the slot feature. All the sketch points should be from the same sketch.

param.name: SlotDirectionType
param.summary: Optional input DirectionTypeEnum that specifies the direction of the slot. When specify this with kCustomDirection, the SlotDirectionEntity should be specified.

param.name: SlotDirectionEntity
param.summary:
Optional input an entity that defines the direction of the slot. This is required only when the SlotDirectionType is specified as kCustomDirection, otherwise this is ignored.
This can be a WorkPlane or planar Face object with which the axis of the slot is perpendicular, a linear Edge, SletchLine, SketchLine3D or WorkAxis object with which the axis of the slot is parallel, a cylindrical/hemispherical/toroidal/conical Face object with which the axis of the slot is parallel to the axis of the face.

param.name: Rotation
param.summary:
Optional input Double or String value specifying the slot rotation angle.
This can be a double or a string. If a double is input, the units are radians. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current angle units of the document. When using a string you can also define equations and reference existing parameters. For example, the string “MyAngle * 2” is valid, assuming there is a parameter named MyAngle.
This defaults to 0 if not specified.

param.name: FlipRotation
param.summary:
Optional input Boolean value specifying if slot rotation is flipped or not.
This defaults to False if not specified.

If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document. This is ignored if the SeatType is not specified as kCountersinkSeat.
Name = CountersinkAngle. Value = A numeric value or a string that specifies the countersink angle. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are radians. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current angle units of the document. This is ignored if the SeatType is not specified as kCountersinkSeat.
Name = SpotfaceWidth. Value = A numeric value or a string that specifies the spotface width. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document. This is ignored if the SeatType is not specified as kSpotfaceSeat.
Name = SpotfaceDepth. Value = A numeric value or a string that specifies the spotface depth. A parameter for this value will be created and the supplied string or value is assigned to the parameter. If a value is input, the units are centimeters. If a string is input, the units can be specified as part of the string or it will default to the current length units of the document. This is ignored if the SeatType is not specified as kSpotfaceSeat.

member.name: M:Inventor.SolidSweepDefinition.SetOrientationInfo(Inventor.SweepProfileOrientationEnum,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that sets the orientation info.

param.name: Orientation
param.summary: Input SweepProfileOrientationEnum to set the orientation of the sweep.

param.name: AlignToVector
param.summary: Optional input object to specify the align to vector. This is required if the Orientation is specified to kAlignToVector. This can be a linear Edge, WorkAxis, WorkPlane or Face which can infer an axis. When a WorkPlane or planar Face object is specified, its normal is used, when a cylindrical, conical, elliptical or toroidal Face is specified its axis is used.

member.name: M:Inventor.SolidSweepDefinition.SetTwistInfo(System.Object,System.Object)
member.summary: Method that sets the twist angle info.

param.name: TwistAngle
param.summary: Input numeric or string value to set the twist angle, a parameter will be created for the twist angle when the sweep is created. If a numeric value is supplied, the value is in radian. If a string value is supplied it will be used as the expression for the newly created parameter, if the value is supplied without a unit qualifier it will default to the current document angle unit. The following is a valid entry for it, assuming the parameter d1 already exists and defines a angle “d1+3 deg”.

param.name: TwistAxis
param.summary: Optional input object to specify the twist axis. This is required if the TwistAngle is specified with non-zero value. This can be a linear Edge, WorkAxis or Face which can infer an axis. When a Face object is specified it should be a cylindrical, conical, elliptical or toroidal surface where its axis is used.

member.name: M:Inventor.SurfaceBody.CalculateFacets(System.Double,System.Int32@,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@,System.Double[]@,System.Int32[]@)
member.summary: Obtain the facetted representation for the given chord-height tolerance. If stored facets available for this tolerance, then those are returned.

param.name: Tolerance
param.summary:
Input Double that specifies the maximum distance that the facet can deviate from the smooth surface. This value is in centimeters. Smaller values can result in a much greater number of facets being returned and will require more processing time to calculate. The picture below illustrates how the chordal tolerance is used when creating a stroked version of a curve. The chordal tolerance defines the maximum distance a line can be from the actual curve. When calculating facets the same concept applies but it defines the maximum distance between a triangle facet and the smooth surface.
The pictures below illustrate the difference obtained when calculating facets for a model using different chordal tolerances. The overall size of this model is approx. 6x6x4 cm’s. The picture on the left used a chordal tolerance of 0.1 cm and the one on the right used a tolerance of 0.01 cm.

param.name: VertexCount
param.summary: Output Long that returns the number of vertices that were generated. This is the number of vertices that will be returned by the VertexCoordinates argument.

param.name: FacetCount
param.summary: Output Long that returns the number of facets that were generated.

param.name: VertexCoordinates
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that contains the coordinate locations of the vertices. The values are defined in x, y, z order within the array and represent coordinates within the model space of the faceted object.

param.name: NormalVectors
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that defines the normal for each vertex in the facet mesh. The values are defined in x, y, z order within the array and represent vector components within the model space of the faceted object.

param.name: VertexIndices
param.summary: Output array of Longs that are used as index values to index into the vertex coordinate list. The first coordinate in the vertex coordinate list is index 1. Using vertex indices allows vertex coordinates to be reused by more than one triangle, thus reducing the overall resources required to define the entire mesh.

member.name: M:Inventor.SurfaceBody.CalculateFacetsWithOptions(System.Double,Inventor.NameValueMap,System.Int32@,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@,System.Double[]@,System.Int32[]@,System.Object@)
member.summary: Method that creates a new set of facets within the specified conditions.

param.name: ChordalTolerance
param.summary: Input Double that specifies the maximum distance that the facet can deviate from the smooth surface. This value is in centimeters. Smaller values can result in a much greater number of facets being returned and will require more processing time to calculate.

param.name: Options
param.summary: Input NameValueMap that specifies additional tolerances that can be used to control the output mesh. The supported options are: Name: MaxSideLength, Value: Defines the maximum side of any triangle in the mesh. A value of 0, or not supplying this value indicates that no maximum length is specified. Name: MaxAspectRatio, Value: Defines the maximum length to height ratio that a triangle can have. This helps to avoid long skinny triangles. A value of 0, or not supplying this value indicates that no maximum aspect ratio is specified. Name: MaxNormalDeviation, Value: Defines the maximum deviation between adjacent vertex normals. This value is the maximum angle allows between normals and is input as radians. A value of 0, or not supplying this value indicates that no normal deviation is specified. Name: ConversionMode, Value: Specifies the conversion mode (0 or 2). 0 - Do not convert the display mesh to a Quad-Dominant mesh. This mode instructs the faceter to keep the generated display mesh (i.e., skip the tri-mesh to quad-dominant mesh conversion). 2 - Convert the triangular display mesh to a triangular mesh suitable for STL output, 3D printing or other similar application requiring a slightly higher quality triangular mesh.

param.name: VertexCount
param.summary: Output Long that specifies the number of vertices in the facet mesh.

param.name: FacetCount
param.summary: Output Long that specifies the number facets in the mesh.

param.name: VertexCoordinates
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that contains the coordinate locations of the vertices. The values are defined in x, y, z order within the array and represent coordinates within the model space of the faceted object.

param.name: NormalVectors
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that defines the normal for each vertex in the facet mesh. The values are defined in x, y, z order within the array and represent vector components within the model space of the faceted object.

param.name: VertexIndices
param.summary: Output array of Longs that are used as index values to index into the vertex coordinate list. The first coordinate in the vertex coordinate list is index 1. Using vertex indices allows vertex coordinates to be reused by more than one triangle, thus reducing the overall resources required to define the entire mesh.

param.name: TextureCoordinates
param.summary: Optional output array of Doubles that defines the texture coordinates that Inventor uses to map the render style texture to the face.

member.name: M:Inventor.SurfaceBody.FindUsingRay(Inventor.Point,Inventor.UnitVector,System.Double,Inventor.ObjectsEnumerator@,Inventor.ObjectsEnumerator@,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Please note: As of Autodesk Inventor 5.3 Service Pack 2, the FindUsingRay method below has superseded LocateUsingRay. Please update your applications accordingly. Method that fires a ray through the part or assembly and returns the entities intersected by the ray. The objects intersected by the ray are returned in the order in which they are intersected, with the first entities returned being those closest to the clipping plane. There is also a precedence in the type of entities returned. The entities returned can be Vertex, Edge, or Face objects. The precedence is in that order. If the ray intersects a vertex, then that vertex is returned and none of the edges or faces that connect to that vertex are returned. If the ray intersects an edge, then that edge is returned and none of the faces that connect to the edge are returned. If the ray intersects a face, then that face is returned. If desired, you can use the functionality provided by the B-Rep portion of the API to obtain the various associated objects from the entity returned. For example if you need a face but an edge is returned, you can use the Faces property of the Edge object to get the associated faces. The start point defines the physical starting point from which to determine intersections. Any intersections behind the start point are ignored. However, the ray is infinite from the start point, so all intersections in the direction of the ray will be returned.

param.name: RayStartPoint
param.summary: Input Point object that defines the start point of the ray in model space.

param.name: RayDirection
param.summary: Input UnitVector object that defines the direction of the ray. The ray is infinite in the direction defined.

param.name: Radius
param.summary: Input Double that defines the radius of the ray. This value is specified in centimeters. Defining a radius for a ray allows the intersection to be within a given tolerance. This radius essentially results in the definition of a cylinder whose axis lies along the axis defined by the RayStartPoint and RayDirection. The intersection result is between the cylinder and the model's entities. A value higher than zero is recommended, though not explicitly required.

param.name: FoundEntities
param.summary: Output ObjectsEnumerator that returns the entities that were intersected by the ray.

param.name: LocationPoints
param.summary: Output ObjectsEnumerator that returns a set of Point objects. One Point object is returned for each entity in the FoundEntities list. The point defines the coordinate of the intersection between the ray and the corresponding entity.

param.name: FindFirstOnly
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether to find just the first entity in the ray's path. If False (the default) then all entities found are returned.

member.name: M:Inventor.SurfaceBody.GetExistingStrokes(System.Double,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@,System.Int32@,System.Int32[]@)
member.summary: Method that returns the specified set of strokes from the SurfaceBody, Face or Edge the method was called from. Existing strokes are stored to single-precision floating point accuracy. This is typically adequate accuracy for display purposes. If a more accurate result is required you can use the CalculateStrokes method, which will calculate new strokes to a given tolerance at double-precision accuracy. If you are using this method within Apprentice, you can use the DisplayAffinity property to optimize Apprentice for access to strokes. member.name: M:Inventor.SurfaceBodyProxy.CalculateFacets(System.Double,System.Int32@,System.Int32@,System.Double[]@,System.Double[]@,System.Int32[]@)
member.summary: Obtain the facetted representation for the given chord-height tolerance. If stored facets available for this tolerance, then those are returned.

param.name: Tolerance
param.summary:
Input Double that specifies the maximum distance that the facet can deviate from the smooth surface. This value is in centimeters. Smaller values can result in a much greater number of facets being returned and will require more processing time to calculate. The picture below illustrates how the chordal tolerance is used when creating a stroked version of a curve. The chordal tolerance defines the maximum distance a line can be from the actual curve. When calculating facets the same concept applies but it defines the maximum distance between a triangle facet and the smooth surface.
The pictures below illustrate the difference obtained when calculating facets for a model using different chordal tolerances. The overall size of this model is approx. 6x6x4 cm’s. The picture on the left used a chordal tolerance of 0.1 cm and the one on the right used a tolerance of 0.01 cm.

param.name: VertexCount
param.summary: Output Long that returns the number of vertices that were generated. This is the number of vertices that will be returned by the VertexCoordinates argument.

param.name: FacetCount
param.summary: Output Long that returns the number of facets that were generated.

param.name: VertexCoordinates
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that contains the coordinate locations of the vertices. The values are defined in x, y, z order within the array and represent coordinates within the model space of the faceted object.

param.name: NormalVectors
param.summary: Output array of Doubles that defines the normal for each vertex in the facet mesh. The values are defined in x, y, z order within the array and represent vector components within the model space of the faceted object.

param.name: VertexIndices
param.summary: Output array of Longs that are used as index values to index into the vertex coordinate list. The first coordinate in the vertex coordinate list is index 1. Using vertex indices allows vertex coordinates to be reused by more than one triangle, thus reducing the overall resources required to define the entire mesh.

member.summary: Method that creates a new set of facets within the specified conditions.

param.name: ChordalTolerance
param.summary: Input Double that specifies the maximum distance that the facet can deviate from the smooth surface. This value is in centimeters. Smaller values can result in a much greater number of facets being returned and will require more processing time to calculate.

param.name: Options
param.summary: Input NameValueMap that specifies additional tolerances that can be used to control the output mesh. The supported options are: Name: MaxSideLength, Value: Defines the maximum side of any triangle in the mesh. A value of 0, or not supplying this value indicates that no maximum length is specified. Name: MaxAspectRatio, Value: Defines the maximum length to height ratio that a triangle can have. This helps to avoid long skinny triangles. A value of 0, or not supplying this value indicates that no maximum aspect ratio is specified. Name: MaxNormalDeviation, Value: Defines the maximum deviation between adjacent vertex normals. This value is the maximum angle allows between normals and is input as radians. A value of 0, or not supplying this value indicates that no normal deviation is specified. Name: ConversionMode, Value: Specifies the conversion mode (0 or 2). 0 - Do not convert the display mesh to a Quad-Dominant mesh. This mode instructs the faceter to keep the generated display mesh (i.e., skip the tri-mesh to quad-dominant mesh conversion). 2 - Convert the triangular display mesh to a triangular mesh suitable for STL output, 3D printing or other similar application requiring a slightly higher quality triangular mesh.

member.name: M:Inventor.SurfaceBodyProxy.FindUsingRay(Inventor.Point,Inventor.UnitVector,System.Double,Inventor.ObjectsEnumerator@,Inventor.ObjectsEnumerator@,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Please note: As of Autodesk Inventor 5.3 Service Pack 2, the FindUsingRay method below has superseded LocateUsingRay. Please update your applications accordingly. Method that fires a ray through the part or assembly and returns the entities intersected by the ray. The objects intersected by the ray are returned in the order in which they are intersected, with the first entities returned being those closest to the clipping plane. There is also a precedence in the type of entities returned. The entities returned can be Vertex, Edge, or Face objects. The precedence is in that order. If the ray intersects a vertex, then that vertex is returned and none of the edges or faces that connect to that vertex are returned. If the ray intersects an edge, then that edge is returned and none of the faces that connect to the edge are returned. If the ray intersects a face, then that face is returned. If desired, you can use the functionality provided by the B-Rep portion of the API to obtain the various associated objects from the entity returned. For example if you need a face but an edge is returned, you can use the Faces property of the Edge object to get the associated faces. The start point defines the physical starting point from which to determine intersections. Any intersections behind the start point are ignored. However, the ray is infinite from the start point, so all intersections in the direction of the ray will be returned.

param.name: RayStartPoint
param.summary: Input Point object that defines the start point of the ray in model space.

param.name: RayDirection
param.summary: Input UnitVector object that defines the direction of the ray. The ray is infinite in the direction defined.

param.name: Radius
param.summary: Input Double that defines the radius of the ray. This value is specified in centimeters. Defining a radius for a ray allows the intersection to be within a given tolerance. This radius essentially results in the definition of a cylinder whose axis lies along the axis defined by the RayStartPoint and RayDirection. The intersection result is between the cylinder and the model's entities. A value higher than zero is recommended, though not explicitly required.

param.name: FoundEntities
param.summary: Output ObjectsEnumerator that returns the entities that were intersected by the ray.

param.name: LocationPoints
param.summary: Output ObjectsEnumerator that returns a set of Point objects. One Point object is returned for each entity in the FoundEntities list. The point defines the coordinate of the intersection between the ray and the corresponding entity.

param.name: FindFirstOnly
param.summary: Optional input Boolean that specifies whether to find just the first entity in the ray's path. If False (the default) then all entities found are returned.
